The Urantia Book says that prayer is not a means of turning God's mind in order to get what we want, but an effort to adjust the human personality to the will of God. "⟦Q 91:8.2⟧Magic was an attempt to adjust Deity to conditions; prayer is the effort to adjust the personality to the will of Deity⟦/Q⟧." [91:8.2] Prayer does not change God, but it works great and lasting changes in the one who prays, and God answers with ever larger revelations of truth, beauty, and goodness. [91:4.5, 91:8.11]

1. Why Is Prayer Necessary?

Real prayer attains reality. The book uses this image: "⟦Q 91:8.9⟧Even when the air currents are ascending, no bird can soar except by outstretched wings⟦/Q⟧." [91:8.9] Prayer is a technique of using the ascending spiritual currents of the universe; it augments spiritual growth, modifies attitudes, and yields the satisfaction that comes from communion with divinity. [91:8.9-8.10] Prayer is a subjective act, yet it contacts mighty objective realities, and it is the most potent stimulus to spiritual growth. [91:8.11]

Prayer has fostered in evolving mankind peace of mind, cheerfulness, calmness, courage, self-mastery, and fair-mindedness. [91:4.5] And sincere prayer of faith is a mighty force for the promotion of personal happiness, individual self-control, social harmony, moral progress, and spiritual attainment. [91:6.3]

2. The Limits of Prayer

Prayer cannot directly affect the physical environment unless it is linked with the will of the spiritual forces and the material supervisors. [91:6.1] Prayer is not a technique for curing real organic disease, but it has contributed greatly to the cure of mental and emotional illness and has enhanced the effect of other treatments. [91:6.2] So the book says, "⟦Q 91:6.5⟧Do not be so slothful as to ask God to solve your difficulties⟦/Q⟧" [91:6.5], and urges us instead to ask for wisdom and spiritual strength while we grapple with our problems.

3. Ethical Prayer

Prayer that seeks selfish advantage over one's fellows cannot be ethical, and such prayer degenerates into pseudo magic. [91:4.1] Prayer must never become a substitute for action; all ethical prayer is a stimulus to action. [91:4.2] We must be fair in prayer and not expect God to love us more than our friends, neighbors, or even enemies. [91:4.3] "⟦Q 91:8.13⟧Pray only for values, not things; for growth, not for gratification⟦/Q⟧." [91:8.13]

4. Conversation with the Indwelling Adjuster

Prayer began as primitive man's conversation with an imagined "other self" and was finally sublimated into true communion with the Paradise Father. [91:3.3-3.4] As the most effective technique for practical purposes, the book says that we should recognize the truth that this other self is now God indwelling us in the factual presence of the Adjuster, so that we "⟦Q 91:3.7⟧can talk face to face, as it were⟦/Q⟧" [91:3.7], with him. God answers the soul's attitude, not the words. [91:8.12]

5. Seven Conditions of Effective Prayer

The book gives seven laws of successful petitioning. [91:9.1]

First, cosmic stamina that sincerely and courageously meets the problems of universe reality. [91:9.2]

Second, the diligence that honestly exhausts every possibility of human adjustment. [91:9.3]

Third, surrendering the wishes of mind and the cravings of soul to the transforming embrace of spiritual growth. [91:9.4]

Fourth, a wholehearted choice of the divine will, without indecision. [91:9.5]

Fifth, unreserved dedication to the actual doing of the Father's will. [91:9.6]

Sixth, concentrating on seeking divine wisdom to solve the specific problems met in the Paradise ascension. [91:9.7]

Seventh, having "faith—living faith" [91:9.8].

Summary

Prayer is not an art of persuading God but an effort to adjust oneself to the will of God, and as a result the one who prays is changed and grows. [91:8.2, 91:4.5] Effective prayer has as its conditions courage and diligence, the choosing and doing of the divine will, the seeking of wisdom for the ascent, and living faith. [91:9.2-9.8] It is worth remembering the saying that only a spiritual child would try to change God. [91:8.8]

q258.question: What are the five "epochal revelations" spoken of in The Urantia Book, and what is the relation between evolutionary religion and revealed religion?
q258.answer:
The Urantia Book says that there have been many religious revelations on Urantia, but only five of epochal significance: the Dalamatian teachings, the Edenic teachings, Melchizedek of Salem, Jesus of Nazareth, and the Urantia Papers. [92:4.4-4.9] Revelation does not abandon evolutionary religion; it sorts, censors, and uplifts it, and so it always keeps in touch with evolution, adapted to man's capacity of receptivity. [92:4.1]

1. The Relation between Evolutionary Religion and Revealed Religion

Evolutionary religion is an emotional reaction born of the realization and fear of the unknown, while revealed religion is the response of the real spiritual world to the human hunger to believe in and depend upon the Deities. "⟦Q 92:4.3⟧Evolutionary religion pictures the circuitous gropings of humanity in quest of truth; revelatory religion is that very truth⟦/Q⟧." [92:4.3] Revealed religion is always characterized by belief in a Deity of final value and by the concept of the survival of personal identity after death. [92:4.2]

But "⟦Q 92:4.1⟧revelation is evolutionary but always progressive⟦/Q⟧" [92:4.1]. If revelation is to exalt evolutionary religion, it must not be too far removed from the thought of its age, so religion by revelation is always limited by man's capacity of receptivity. [92:4.1]

2. The First Revelation: The Dalamatian Teachings

The true concept of the First Source and Center was first proclaimed by the one hundred corporeal members of the staff of Caligastia, the Planetary Prince. This revelation continued for more than three hundred thousand years but was abruptly terminated by the planetary rebellion and the disruption of the teaching regime. [92:4.5] Except for the work of Van, its influence was practically lost, and the red men retained it longest. [92:4.5]

3. The Second Revelation: The Edenic Teachings

Adam and Eve again presented the concept of the Father of all to the evolutionary peoples, but the disruption of the first Eden halted the revelation before it had fully begun. Their teachings were carried on by the Sethite priests and changed the course of religious evolution in the Levant, but by 2500 B.C. mankind had largely lost sight of them. [92:4.6]

4. The Third Revelation: Melchizedek of Salem

Melchizedek, the emergency Son of Nebadon, made trust and faith his basic precepts, teaching men to trust in the almighty beneficence of God, and proclaimed that faith was the act by which men earned God's favor. [92:4.7] His teachings became mingled with various evolutionary religions and developed into the theologic systems of the first millennium after Christ. [92:4.7]

5. The Fourth and Fifth Revelations: Jesus and the Urantia Papers

Christ Michael revealed God as the Universal Father, and the substance of his teaching was love and service: the voluntary worship of love that responds to the Father's love, and the freewill service bestowed upon one's brothers. [92:4.8]

The Urantia Papers are the most recent presentation of truth, and they differ from previous revelations in that they are not the work of a single personality but a composite presentation by many beings. [92:4.9] The book frankly states of itself that "⟦Q 92:4.9⟧no revelation short of the attainment of the Universal Father can ever be complete⟦/Q⟧" [92:4.9], acknowledging that all celestial ministrations are partial and transient.

6. Revelation and Religious Leaders

The concept of God has been formed by a blending of the pre-existing ideas of the evolutionary cults, the sublime ideals of revealed religion, and the viewpoints of the great religious leaders. [92:5.1-5.4] The leaders often became objects of superstitious awe, but they were the fulcrum on which the lever of revealed truth rested. [92:5.7]

Summary

The five epochal revelations are Dalamatia, Eden, Melchizedek, Jesus, and the Urantia Papers, and each in its age enlarged the truth that makes God known as Father. [92:4.4-4.9] Revelation does not so much replace evolutionary religion as purify and uplift it, and it is given progressively within man's capacity of receptivity. [92:4.1] The fact that even The Urantia Book says it is not complete teaches an attitude of humble inquiry. [92:4.9]

q259.question: Who, according to The Urantia Book, is Melchizedek, the king of Salem who appears briefly in Genesis, what did he teach, and where is he now?
q259.answer:
In The Urantia Book, Melchizedek of Salem is Machiventa Melchizedek, an "emergency Son," one of the twelve planetary receivers of Urantia, who volunteered and was incarnated in the temporary likeness of a human being. [93:1.3] He appeared 1,973 years before the birth of Jesus and for ninety-four years taught at Salem the one God and salvation by faith; this was the third epochal revelation to Urantia. [93:2.1, 93:4.16, 92:4.7]

1. Why Did He Come?

For thousands of years after the failure of the Adamic mission, revealed truth was in danger of extinction, and by about 3000 B.C. the concept of God had grown very dim. [93:1.1] The twelve Melchizedek planetary receivers petitioned the Most Highs of Edentia for help but were told to solve the problem themselves, and Machiventa volunteered to do what had been done only six times in all the history of Nebadon: to personalize as a temporary man and bestow himself as an emergency Son. [93:1.2-1.3]

2. What Kind of Being Did He Live As?

He first made his appearance at the tent of Amdon, a Chaldean herder of Sumerian extraction, and soon became known as the priest of El Elyon and the sage of Salem. [93:2.1, 93:2.4] He never married and could not have left offspring; his body was a special physical body like those used by the corporeal staff of Caligastia. [93:2.6] He received a Thought Adjuster, and through this experience the Adjuster gained a practical introduction to the later indwelling of Michael. [93:2.7]

3. What Did He Teach?

The creed of Salem was very simple: to believe in El Elyon, the one Universal Father of all things; to accept the covenant with the Most High, "⟦Q 93:4.3⟧which bestows the favor of God on my faith, not on sacrifices and burnt offerings⟦/Q⟧" [93:4.3]; and to keep the seven commandments and proclaim this good news. [93:4.2-4.4] The second of the seven commandments was, "⟦Q 93:4.8⟧You shall not doubt that faith is the only requirement for eternal salvation⟦/Q⟧." [93:4.8]

No sacrifices were permitted at Salem, and instead of blood sacrifices Melchizedek introduced the sacrament of bread and wine. [93:4.14] But the people of that day were so firmly set in the belief that man is born in debt to the gods that they could hardly grasp the idea of securing God's favor by faith. [93:4.5] He placed all his teaching under the doctrine of one God, the divine Father, and he taught that another Son of God would come, born of a woman, thus preparing the way for Michael. [93:3.6-3.7]

4. The Covenant with Abraham

Melchizedek made a formal covenant with Abraham at Salem. In this covenant "⟦Q 93:6.4⟧God agrees to do everything; man only agrees to believe God's promises and follow his instructions⟦/Q⟧." [93:6.4] Until then it had been believed that salvation could be secured only by sacrifices and offerings, but now the good news was proclaimed that God's favor is to be had by faith. [93:6.4] To commemorate this, Abraham changed his name from Abram to Abraham. [93:6.5]

5. His Departure and Present Status

For several reasons, including the people's tendency to regard him as a demigod, he decided to end his bestowal soon after the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah. [93:8.1] On the third day after his disappearance from Salem he reappeared among his fellow receivers. [93:10.1] For the next nineteen centuries he co-operated with the prophets to preserve the truths of Salem [93:10.4]; after Michael's triumph he became one of the twenty-four directors on Jerusem, and recently he received the title of "⟦Q 93:10.5⟧vicegerent Planetary Prince of Urantia⟦/Q⟧." [93:10.5] The book reports that there have been rulings strongly suggesting that he is destined to take the place of the fallen Caligastia. [93:10.6]

Summary

Machiventa Melchizedek is the emergency Son who volunteered to incarnate in an age when the light of truth was going out; he taught the one God and favor through faith and made a covenant with Abraham, preparing the way for Michael. [93:1.3, 93:3.8, 93:6.4] Today, as vicegerent Planetary Prince of Urantia, he may come to play an important part in the future of this world. [93:10.5, 93:10.11]

q260.question: What relation did Lao-tse, Confucius, and Gautama Siddhartha of the sixth century B.C. have to Melchizedek's Salem teachings, and what did each of them teach?
q260.answer:
The Urantia Book regards the sixth century B.C. as a remarkable century in which the Salem gospel was proclaimed anew through several human teachers. Melchizedek saw the pure doctrines he had taught being endangered by absorption into the older beliefs, and through the co-ordination of spiritual agencies not fully understood even by the planetary supervisors, Urantia witnessed an unprecedented presentation of religious truth. [94:6.1] Lao-tse and Confucius in China and Gautama Siddhartha in India were its representative teachers. [94:6.2, 94:7.1]

1. Lao-tse: Tao and Everlasting Union

Lao-tse "⟦Q 94:6.3⟧built directly upon the concepts of the Salem traditions⟦/Q⟧" [94:6.3] when he declared Tao to be the One First Cause of all creation, and he taught that man's eternal destiny was everlasting union with Tao, Supreme God and Universal King. [94:6.3] He was one of the first to set forth the doctrine of returning good for evil, and he likened true faith to the "⟦Q 94:6.5⟧attitude of a little child⟦/Q⟧." [94:6.4-6.5] His doctrine of nonresistance was later distorted into the belief in doing nothing, but Lao-tse never taught such error. [94:6.7] Present-day popular Taoism has very little in common with the lofty cosmic concepts of this philosopher. [94:6.8]

2. Confucius: Morality and Order

Confucius was a younger contemporary of Lao; he based his doctrines on the long moral traditions of the yellow race and was also somewhat influenced by the traditions of the Salem missionaries. He set a new pace by putting morality in the place of magic, but "⟦Q 94:6.9⟧he built too well; he made a new fetish out of order⟦/Q⟧" [94:6.9] and established a respect for ancestral conduct. His writings became the moral foundation of the culture of almost one third of Urantia's population, but they were somewhat inimical to the investigative spirit of the Chinese. [94:6.11] Mo Ti, who proclaimed a brotherhood based on the love of God, opposed this but was frustrated. [94:6.11]

3. Gautama Siddhartha: A Gospel Close to Salvation by Faith

Gautama decried the practice of seeking salvation through physical suffering, and he fought against the caste system. [94:7.2] At Benares his disciple Bautan passed on to him the traditions of Melchizedek's covenant with Abraham, and although he did not have a clear concept of the Universal Father, he took an advanced stand on salvation through faith and sent his disciples out to proclaim the "good news" of a freely given salvation. [94:7.5] His gospel of universal salvation, free from sacrifice, ritual, and priests, "⟦Q 94:7.7⟧came surprisingly near to being a revival of the Salem gospel⟦/Q⟧" [94:7.7].

But he did not grasp the personality of the One Universal Being, and he failed to present a way to Paradise. [94:7.3] In later years his son and successor wavered from the Salem gospel of divine favor through faith alone, and his dying words in old age were, "⟦Q 94:7.6⟧Work out your own salvation⟦/Q⟧." [94:7.6] In the original teaching, salvation is achieved by human effort apart from divine help, and the book judges it to be "⟦Q 94:8.18⟧the best godless philosophy ever invented by mortal man⟦/Q⟧" and the ideal humanism. [94:8.17-8.18] Its greatest weakness was that it failed to become a religion of unselfish social service. [94:8.19]

4. A Common Fate: Distortion and Deification

Confucius and Lao-tse were eventually raised to the status of gods by their followers. [94:6.12] The book also says that "⟦Q 94:7.8⟧Modern Buddhism is no more the teachings of Gautama Siddhartha than is Christianity the teachings of Jesus of Nazareth⟦/Q⟧" [94:7.8], placing it side by side with the fact that modern Christianity is not the original teaching of Jesus.

Summary

The great teachers of the East in the sixth century B.C. each revived in his own way the fading Salem gospel. [94:6.1] Lao-tse taught union with Tao built directly on the Salem traditions, Confucius taught morality and order, and Gautama taught a universal salvation close to the Salem gospel. [94:6.3, 94:6.9, 94:7.7] But because they lacked a clear concept of a personal Universal Father, or because their teachings were later distorted, that light had to await the bestowal of Michael. [94:7.3, 94:6.12]

q261.question: Who was the Egyptian Pharaoh Ikhnaton, why did his monotheistic reform fail, and what did it leave behind?
q261.answer:
The Urantia Book regards Ikhnaton as "⟦Q 95:5.2⟧one of the most remarkable persons in human history⟦/Q⟧." [95:5.2] Since Melchizedek, no human being up to that time had so clearly understood the revealed religion of Salem, and at a time of spiritual depression in Mesopotamia he kept alive in Egypt the doctrine of El Elyon, the One God, thus maintaining the monotheistic channel for the bestowal of Michael. [95:5.2] But because he went too fast and too far ahead, his reform failed in his own day. [95:5.4, 95:5.12]

1. How Did He Come to Know the One God?

As the teachings of Amenemope were fading, a woman of the royal family accepted the teachings of Melchizedek through the influence of a Salemite physician in Egypt, and she persuaded her son Ikhnaton to accept the doctrine of the One God. [95:5.1] The earlier teacher Amenemope had exalted conscience as the supreme standard of right and wrong and taught that God-consciousness is the deciding factor in all conduct. [95:4.1-4.2]

2. Monotheism Hidden under the Guise of the Sun-god

Ikhnaton attempted more systematically than any other king in history to change a whole nation from polytheism to monotheism. He broke with the past, changed his name, abandoned the capital, built a new city, and created a new art and literature. [95:5.4] On the advice of the Salemite physician he sought to approach the worship of the Universal Father by absorbing all the gods into the worship of the sun [95:5.6], and while maintaining the outward worship of Aton he led the people to worship "⟦Q 95:5.7⟧the One God, creator of Aton and supreme Father of all⟦/Q⟧." [95:5.7]

He wrote a book of thirty-one chapters entitled "The One God," but when the priests returned to power they utterly destroyed it; of his one hundred and thirty-seven hymns, twelve are preserved in the Old Testament Book of Psalms. [95:5.7] The supreme word of his religion was "righteousness." [95:5.8]

3. Why Did It Fail?

A reform that went too fast: He built more than could stand after he was gone, and he failed to provide adequately for the material security and prosperity of his people. [95:5.4]

Lack of political genius: It is said that if he had possessed the political sagacity of Moses, he would have changed the history of Occidental religion. [95:5.3, 95:5.5]

Resistance of the priests: The priests secretly kept up their cults and resumed their activities soon after he was gone, and they blamed all of Egypt's troubles on monotheism. [95:5.5]

A concept of God that was too high: His greatest truth, that Aton was the creator of the whole world, was not nationalistic, so it did not raise the morale of the army and handed the priests a weapon. [95:5.9] Moreover only the educated could understand it, and the peasants returned to the worship of Isis and Osiris. [95:5.12]

4. What He Left Behind

His son-in-law returned to the old gods and changed his name to Tutankhamen [95:5.10], but the priests never fully overcame the tide of monotheism and had to combine the gods more and more, and the concept of one God never disappeared from Egypt or the world. [95:5.11] The democracy of salvation and resurrection that he taught finally triumphed. [95:5.13] The aftermath of his work persisted for centuries in Palestine and Greece, and the Hebrew Bedouins sojourning in Egypt perpetuated many of his doctrines in their own religion. [95:5.14-5.15] It was partly in recognition of this exploit that the child Jesus was taken to Egypt, where some of the spiritual successors of Ikhnaton saw him. [95:5.2]

Summary

Ikhnaton was the king who most clearly understood the Salem truth of the One God, and he tried to establish the worship of the Universal Father under the guise of the sun-god. [95:5.2, 95:5.6-5.7] His reform, too fast and too lofty, collapsed in his own day, but his concept of the One God passed on to the Hebrews and the Western world and became part of the background for the bestowal of Michael. [95:5.11, 95:5.14-5.15]

q262.question: How does The Urantia Book use the relation between Moses and Yahweh to explain why the God of the Old Testament is portrayed as jealous and wrathful?
q262.answer:
According to The Urantia Book, Moses knew the lofty concept of El Elyon, the one Most High God, which came from the Melchizedek tradition. But because the ignorant Bedouin slaves could not understand it, he chose the compromise of presenting his new and higher concept of God under the name of their old tribal god, "Yahweh." [96:4.2-4.3] The book explains that the portrayal of the Old Testament God as jealous and wrathful is due to this compromise and to the limited understanding of the people Moses taught. [96:4.7]

1. What Kind of Man Was Moses?

Moses' mother was of the Egyptian royal family, and his father was a Semitic liaison officer. [96:3.1] He was "⟦Q 96:5.1⟧the most important individual world teacher and leader between the times of Machiventa and Jesus⟦/Q⟧" [96:5.1], at once military leader, social organizer, and religious teacher. The Bedouin captives he led had no real concept of God and no hope. [96:3.2-3.3]

2. From El Elyon to Yahweh

Moses had heard the teachings of Machiventa Melchizedek from both his parents; his parents believed in El Shaddai, and his Kenite father-in-law worshiped El Elyon. From all these beliefs he formed an enlarged concept of Deity, and he judged it wise to proclaim it as an expanded concept of the old tribal god Yahweh. [96:4.2] For although he had tried to teach the idea of El Elyon, he was convinced that the people would never comprehend it. [96:4.3] But since Yahweh had long been symbolized by the golden calf of the Bedouin tribes, he was plagued by the awkward predicament of presenting a new idea under the old term. [96:4.3]

3. The Eruption at Sinai and the "Fearful God"

During the third week of their sojourn at the foot of Sinai, Horeb erupted violently, and because of this cataclysm Moses was able to impress upon the people the teaching that God was mighty and terrible, "a devouring fire." [96:4.5] Because he was building a new nation, he nationalized his teachings and spoke of Yahweh as a hard taskmaster, a "jealous God." [96:4.6] Moses also feared to proclaim the mercy of Yahweh, preferring to hold his people in awe through fear of God's justice. [96:5.6] So the Hebrews of this time learned little of the mercy of God and learned of him as a "man of war," a God of battles. [96:5.7]

4. Nevertheless, the Lofty God Moses Pointed To

At the same time Moses sought to enlarge their concept by teaching that Yahweh was the God of the spirits of all flesh and a covenant-keeping God. [96:4.6] He also presented Yahweh as a God of truth and without iniquity, trying to exalt him to the dignity of supreme Deity, but because of the limited understanding of his followers he had to speak of God in the image of man, as having anger, wrath, and vengefulness. [96:4.7] To the assembled leaders he proclaimed that the Lord God is one and there is none beside him. [96:5.5]

5. The Retreat after Moses and the Long Evolution

When Moses died, his lofty concepts rapidly declined, and the people went back to the old ideas of the desert and the worship of the golden calf. [96:5.8, 96:6.1] Yet the book says that the most remarkable feature of Hebrew religious history is precisely the continuous evolution of the concept of Deity, from the primitive god of Mount Horeb up to the teachings of the Isaiahs, who proclaimed God as the loving and merciful Creator Father. [96:4.9] The captivity finally liberated the concept of Yahweh to take on the monotheistic role of God of all peoples. [96:4.8]

Summary

The Old Testament picture of a jealous and wrathful God is not so much God's real character as the result of Moses conveying the lofty concept of El Elyon to an ignorant people under the name of the tribal god Yahweh, putting justice and fear in the foreground. [96:4.3, 96:4.6-4.7, 96:5.6] This concept later grew, through the prophets, into the concept of a loving Father. [96:4.9] Therefore when we read the Old Testament, we should also keep in view the fact that the concept of God evolved progressively.

q263.question: How did the Hebrew concept of God develop through the prophets from Samuel to the second Isaiah?
q263.answer:
The Urantia Book credits the spiritual leaders of the Hebrews with the unique achievement of deanthropomorphizing the concept of God without turning it into an abstraction that only philosophers could understand. [97:0.1] From Moses to Malachi the idea of the personality of God grew almost without interruption, and this concept was finally glorified in Jesus' teachings about the Father in heaven. [97:0.2] Each prophet added a new attribute to the earlier concept.

1. Samuel: The Changeless God

Samuel came from a long line of Salem teachers. [97:1.2] His great contribution was the pronouncement that Yahweh was changeless, forever the same embodiment of perfection. At that time Yahweh was thought of as a fitful God, always regretting what he had done, but under Samuel's teaching he began the ascent from the level of a tribal god to the ideal of "⟦Q 97:1.4⟧an all-powerful and changeless Creator and Supervisor of all creation⟦/Q⟧." [97:1.4] Yet Samuel did not get far beyond the tribal concept of a Yahweh concerned chiefly with his chosen people. [97:1.7]

2. Elijah and Elisha: Restoration

Elijah restored to the northern kingdom a concept of God comparable to that of the days of Samuel, but he was so busy tearing down the altars of Baal that he had little opportunity to present advanced concepts. [97:2.1] This was a period of restoration, not of progress, in the concept of Deity. [97:2.3] Elijah transformed the socioeconomic conflict between the Yahwehites and the Baalites over land into a moral and religious issue. [97:3.1, 97:3.6]

3. Amos and Hosea: Justice and Love

Amos was not merely a reformer; he was "⟦Q 97:4.2⟧a discoverer of new concepts of Deity⟦/Q⟧" [97:4.2]. By proclaiming that Yahweh would not tolerate the sins of his people just because they were chosen, he made a direct attack on the egoistic doctrine of the "chosen people," and he proclaimed Yahweh as the God of all nations. [97:4.2, 97:4.4] Hosea revived Moses' concept of a God of love, preaching forgiveness through repentance, not by sacrifice. [97:4.5] If Amos awakened the national conscience, Hosea sounded the first notes of the chord of divine compassion and loving-kindness. [97:4.7]

4. The First Isaiah, Micah, and Jeremiah: Expansion and Internationalization

The first Isaiah preached the eternal nature of God, his infinite wisdom, and his unchanging reliability. [97:5.2] Micah and Obadiah fearlessly attacked the whole priest-ridden system of ritual and sacrifice. [97:5.4] Jeremiah declared that Yahweh was not on the side of the Hebrews in their military struggles but was God of all the earth and of all nations, and his teaching was "⟦Q 97:6.2⟧the crescendo of the rising wave of the internationalization of the God of Israel⟦/Q⟧" [97:6.2].

5. The Second Isaiah: The Loving Universal Father

The priests of the captivity, out of resentment over their lost national deity, inflated their history [97:7.1], but the young prophet, the second Isaiah, greatly curbed their influence. [97:7.4] "⟦Q 97:7.5⟧No prophet or religious teacher from Machiventa to the time of Jesus attained the high concept of God that Isaiah the second proclaimed during these days of the captivity⟦/Q⟧." [97:7.5] He eclipsed the nationalistic Yahweh and portrayed a God embracing universal justice, divine mercy, and eternal righteousness; he "⟦Q 97:7.13⟧portrayed the all-powerful Creator as the all-loving Father⟦/Q⟧." [97:7.13] The book says that at last Machiventa Melchizedek beheld human teachers proclaiming a real God. [97:7.6]

Summary

The Hebrew concept of God grew from Samuel's 'changeless God,' through Amos's 'God of justice who judges all nations fairly,' Hosea's 'God of love and mercy,' and Jeremiah's 'God of all nations,' to the second Isaiah's 'Universal Father who loves all.' [97:1.4, 97:4.2-4.5, 97:6.2, 97:7.13] This long evolution became the foundation for receiving Jesus' teaching about the Father in heaven. [97:0.2]

q264.question: Christianity and Mithraism are said to resemble each other in many ways. How does The Urantia Book explain the elements from which present-day Christianity was formed?
q264.answer:
The Urantia Book explains that Christianity was formed around the person of Jesus of Nazareth, but that as a system of belief it was made up of a combination of seven elements: the teachings of Melchizedek, Hebrew theology, Zoroastrianism, the mystery cults such as Mithraism, the life of Jesus, the viewpoint of Paul, and Greek philosophy. [98:7.2-7.10] In particular, during the three centuries after Christ, Christianity competed with Mithraism and came to resemble it greatly in outward form and ceremony. [98:6.3]

1. The Mystery Cults and Mithraism

Many people in the Greco-Roman world had lost their primitive family and national religions and could not grasp Greek philosophy, so they turned to the emotional mystery cults of Egypt and the Levant. [98:4.1] The Phrygian and Egyptian mysteries taught that a divine son had died and been raised again, and that the initiates shared in the immortality of that god. [98:4.6] These cults finally gave way to the greatest of the mystery cults, the worship of Mithras, which spread throughout the empire by way of the Roman legions. [98:5.1] It was chiefly through the Mithraic cult that the religion of Zoroaster influenced Christianity. [98:5.2]

2. Familiar Elements within Mithraism

The story of Mithras included a flood from which one man escaped in a boat, and a last supper with the sun-god before his ascension to heaven. [98:5.3] Its devotees held weekly services on the day of the sun-god, and the most elaborate ceremony was the annual festival of Mithras on December twenty-fifth. They believed that partaking of the sacrament assured eternal life, and that at the end of the world Mithras would call forth the dead for the last judgment. [98:5.4]

3. The Resemblances and the Decisive Difference between the Two Religions

In both religions the places of worship were mostly underground, and both had altars depicting the sufferings of a savior who had brought salvation to a sin-cursed human race. [98:6.3] The Mithraic custom of dipping the fingers in holy water passed into the Christian churches in the vicinity of Rome, and both religions employed baptism and partook of the sacrament of bread and wine. [98:6.4]

The differences were clear. The characters of Mithras and Jesus were different, and Mithraism encouraged militarism while Christianity was ultrapacific. And the deciding factor in the competition was "⟦Q 98:6.4⟧the admission of women into the full fellowship of the Christian faith⟦/Q⟧." [98:6.4] Mithraism at first was a religion for men only. [98:5.5]

4. The Seven Elements That Made Up Christianity

The book sums up the elements of Christianity as follows.

The teachings of Melchizedek: the basic factor in all the religions of East and West during the past four thousand years. [98:7.4]

The Hebrew heritage: morals, ethics, theology, and belief in Providence and the supreme Yahweh. [98:7.5]

Zoroastrianism: the concept of the cosmic struggle between good and evil, which through contact with Mithraism strongly influenced the structure of doctrine and cosmology. [98:7.6]

The mystery cults: even the legends of the birth of Jesus became tainted with the Roman version of the birth of Mithras, said to have been witnessed only by gift-bearing shepherds. [98:7.7]

The life of Jesus: the historical life of Joshua ben Joseph and the reality of the glorified Christ. [98:7.8]

The viewpoint of Paul: in Tarsus during his youth Mithraism was dominant, and he never imagined that his letters would later be regarded as "⟦Q 98:7.9⟧the word of God⟦/Q⟧." [98:7.9]

Greek philosophy: combined with Pauline theology, it forms the basis of European ethics to this day. [98:7.10]

In the end, Greek philosophy supplied the concepts of ethical value; Mithraism, the ritual of worship observance; and Christianity, the technique for the conservation of moral and social values. [98:6.5]

5. The Religion of Jesus and the Religion about Jesus

The book stresses that the Creator Son came not to appease an angry God but to lead all mankind to the recognition of the Father's love and of sonship with God. [98:7.1] Christianity has glorified Jesus as the Messiah "⟦Q 98:7.11⟧but has largely forgotten the Master's personal gospel: the Fatherhood of God and the universal brotherhood of all men⟦/Q⟧." [98:7.11]

Summary

Present-day Christianity is a religion that puts Jesus at its center while combining elements from Melchizedek, the Hebrews, Zoroaster, Mithraism, Paul, and Greek philosophy, and it closely resembles Mithraism in outward forms such as the sacrament, baptism, holy water, and the savior's altar. [98:6.3-6.4, 98:7.3-7.10] The Urantia Book urges us to know this history while recovering the gospel of Jesus himself that lies hidden within it: the Fatherhood of God and the brotherhood of man. [98:7.11]

q165.question: What is meant by the statement that Paradise "exists without time and has no location in space"?
q165.answer:
Paradise is the center of the universe and the dwelling place of God, but it is not one more heavenly body bound by the laws of time and space. The Urantia Book says: "⟦Q 11:2.10⟧Paradise exists without time and has no location in space⟦/Q⟧" [11:2.10]. This does not mean that Paradise is set somewhere within space; rather, it means that space and time arise and unfold with Paradise as their point of reference.

In other words, Paradise is less a place within the universe than the absolute point of reference that makes the universe possible. Thus the book calls Paradise "⟦Q 11:9.2⟧the geographic center of infinity⟦/Q⟧" [11:9.2], yet says that it is neither a part of universal creation nor even a real part of the eternal Havona universe, but "⟦Q 11:9.2⟧an eternal and exclusive existence⟦/Q⟧" [11:9.2].

1. Paradise Is Not in Space but Is the Source of Space

Space does not exist on any of the surfaces of Paradise; space does not touch Paradise directly, and only the quiescent midspace zones come in contact with the central Isle [11:7.1]. Space is neither the presence of the Unqualified Absolute nor a function of the Ultimate; "⟦Q 11:7.4⟧it is a bestowal of Paradise⟦/Q⟧" [11:7.4]. Roughly speaking, space seemingly originates just below nether Paradise, and time just above upper Paradise [11:2.11]. Paradise, therefore, is not an object in space but the place from which space proceeds.

2. No Time, Yet a Sequence of Events

Time as we understand it is not a feature of Paradise existence, yet the citizens of the central Isle are fully conscious of the "⟦Q 11:2.11⟧nontime sequence of events⟦/Q⟧" [11:2.11]. Motion, too, is not inherent on Paradise; it is volitional [11:2.11]. To say that there is no time does not mean that nothing happens, but that things happen without being subject to the flow of time. Moreover, the concept of distance, even absolute distance, has very much meaning as it may be applied to relative locations on Paradise [11:2.11].

3. A Unique Source Material: Absolutum

The eternal Isle is composed of a homogeneous organization of space potency not to be found elsewhere in all the universe of universes, and the Melchizedeks of Nebadon named it absolutum [11:2.9]. This Paradise source material is neither dead nor alive; it is the original nonspiritual expression of the First Source and Center [11:2.9]. The Universal Father appears to have concentrated all absolute potential for cosmic reality in Paradise as a means of making possible subinfinite, even time-space, creation [11:2.10]. But it does not follow that Paradise is time-space limited just because the universes disclose time-space qualities [11:2.10].

4. Not Deity, Yet the Source-Center of All Things

When the Father revealed the infinite personality expression of his spirit self in the Eternal Son, he simultaneously revealed the infinite potential of his nonpersonal self as Paradise [11:9.3]. Paradise is therefore nonpersonal and nonspiritual, and the book states plainly that "⟦Q 11:9.4⟧Paradise is not Deity⟦/Q⟧" [11:9.4]. Nevertheless, Paradise is the universal headquarters of all personality activities and the source-center of all force-space and energy manifestations [11:9.7]. Paradise is also the absolute of patterns, and Havona is an exhibit of these potentials in actuality [11:9.5].

5. What It Means for Us

What matters most for mortals is that this dwelling place of the Father, beyond time and space, is the real and far-distant destiny of the immortal souls of ascending creatures [11:9.8]. Every God-knowing mortal who has embraced the career of doing the Father's will has already embarked upon the Paradise journey [11:9.8]. The very fact that we who live in time and space set our goal on a place beyond time and space shows that human destiny is not confined to the material world.

Summary

Paradise is not an island set in space but the nonspatial and timeless center from which space and time proceed [11:2.10, 11:7.4]. There is a sequence of events and meaning of location there, but no flow of time and no limitation of space [11:2.11]. Paradise is not Deity, yet it is the source-center of all energy and personality activity [11:9.4, 11:9.7], and it is the final destination at which every God-knowing mortal will at last arrive [11:9.8].

q166.question: What is the "space respiration" spoken of in The Urantia Book, and what does it mean that space alternately expands and contracts?
q166.answer:
The Urantia Book says that all space is observed alternately to contract and expand, and it calls this "space respiration" [11:6.1]. While the horizontal pervaded space in which the universes are situated expands, the vertical reservoir space above and below Paradise contracts, and vice versa [11:6.2]. Each phase lasts a little more than one billion Urantia years, and a complete cycle of expansion and contraction takes a little more than two billion years [11:6.4-5].

What is noteworthy in this teaching is that the revelators themselves frankly state, "⟦Q 11:6.1⟧We do not know the actual mechanism of space respiration⟦/Q⟧" [11:6.1], and report only the observed facts.

1. Two Kinds of Space: Pervaded Space and Unpervaded Space

Pervaded space: the space that contains the universes, extending horizontally outward from near approach to peripheral Paradise through the fourth outer space level and beyond [11:6.4, 11:7.4]. This space is believed to be actually pervaded by the ancestral space potency of the Unqualified Absolute [11:7.4].

Unpervaded space: space "⟦Q 11:6.3⟧unpervaded by those forces, energies, powers, and presences known to exist in pervaded space⟦/Q⟧" [11:6.3]; these are the reservoirs extending vertically above upper Paradise and below nether Paradise [11:6.4].

The book compares the volume outlines of these reservoirs to an hourglass [11:6.1]. It also says that a vertical cross section of all space would resemble a Maltese cross, the horizontal arms representing pervaded (universe) space and the vertical arms representing unpervaded (reservoir) space [11:7.3].

2. Where the Respiration Takes Place

The junction of pervaded and unpervaded space lies just underneath nether Paradise. Both spaces flow through the transmuting regulation channels there, and in the cycles of contraction and expansion pervadable space is changed into unpervadable space and vice versa [11:6.2]. Yet there is no space on the surfaces of Paradise; only the quiescent midspace zones are in contact with the Isle [11:7.1], and Paradise is the motionless nucleus of the relatively quiet zones existing between pervaded and unpervaded space [11:7.2].

3. Which Phase Are We in Now?

At present, pervaded space is approaching the mid-point of the phase of expansion, while unpervaded space nears the mid-point of the phase of contraction [11:6.4]. Theoretically, the outermost limits of both space extensions are now approximately equidistant from Paradise [11:6.4]. For one billion years, while the force activities of the master universe and of all horizontal space expand, the space reservoirs contract [11:6.5].

4. An Order for Balance and Stability

The book says that it does not know whether reservoir space is destined always to function as the equipoise of universe space, or whether there is a creative intent concerning it, yet it says that the reservoirs seem to counterbalance the expansion-contraction cycles of the universe of universes [11:6.3]. Again, the quiet zones between the space levels and the alternate clockwise and counterclockwise flows of the galaxies are physical gravity stabilizers that keep gravity pressure from accumulating to the point of destructive activities; they exert antigravity influences and act as brakes upon dangerous velocities [11:7.9]. Here we can glimpse how even the rhythms of space are woven in orderly fashion around Paradise.

Summary

Space respiration is a vast cycle in which the horizontal pervaded space containing the universes and the vertical unpervaded space above and below Paradise alternately expand and contract [11:6.1-2]. One phase lasts a little more than a billion years and a whole cycle a little more than two billion years [11:6.4-5], and pervaded space is now approaching the middle of its expansion phase [11:6.4]. Even the revelators do not know its mechanism, but its rhythm is understood as part of the balance and stability of the universe centered on Paradise [11:6.3, 11:7.9].

q167.question: What are the four absolute gravity circuits, personality gravity, spirit gravity, mind gravity, and physical gravity, and how do they differ?
q167.answer:
The Urantia Book says that all forms of force-energy, whether material, mindal, or spiritual, are alike subject to the grasp of that universal presence which we call "gravity," and that personality also is responsive to gravity, to the Father's exclusive circuit [12:3.1]. In other words, gravity is not merely a force by which bodies attract one another; it is a fourfold presence by which the Deities draw all the realities of the universe to themselves.

The four circuits are the personality gravity of the Universal Father, the spirit gravity of the Eternal Son, the mind gravity of the Conjoint Actor, and the cosmic gravity of the Isle of Paradise [12:3.2-5]. These four circuits are not related to the nether Paradise force center; they are not circuits of force, energy, or power, but "⟦Q 12:3.6⟧They are absolute presence circuits and like God are independent of time and space⟦/Q⟧" [12:3.6]. The corps of gravity researchers on Uversa have estimated how much of each circuit is now operating in the universe [12:3.7], and their findings illustrate well the differences among the four circuits.

1. Physical Gravity: The Cosmic Gravity of the Isle of Paradise

According to the researchers' computations, the central universe and the seven superuniverses are at present using only about five per cent of the active functioning of the Paradise absolute-gravity grasp [12:3.8]. The remaining ninety-five per cent or so is engaged in controlling material systems beyond the borders of the present organized universes [12:3.8]. These calculations all refer to absolute gravity; linear gravity is an interactive phenomenon which can be computed only by knowing the actual Paradise gravity [12:3.8].

2. Spirit Gravity: The Drawing Power of the Eternal Son

By the same technique, the total spirit gravity of the Eternal Son was computed and found to be almost exactly equal to the spirit gravity actually functioning in the grand universe [12:3.9]. This means that the universes now evolving in outer space are at present wholly nonspiritual, and it explains why spirit-endowed beings know so little about those vast energy manifestations [12:3.9].

3. Mind Gravity: The Intellectual Drawing of the Conjoint Actor

The researchers averaged three types of material mind and three types of spiritual mind to obtain a unit of mind estimation [12:3.10], and they deduced that about eighty-five per cent of the mind-gravity response originates in the existing grand universe [12:3.10]. The remainder suggests the possibility that mind activities are connected with the physical activities in outer space, which agrees with the belief that intelligent force organizers are directing universe evolution beyond the grand universe. That intelligence, however, appears not to be responsive to spirit gravity [12:3.10]. All these computations are estimates based on assumed laws, yet they are said to be fairly reliable [12:3.11].

4. Personality Gravity: The Father's Exclusive Circuit

"⟦Q 12:3.12⟧Personality Gravity is noncomputable⟦/Q⟧" [12:3.12]. The circuit is recognized, but the realities responsive to it cannot be measured either qualitatively or quantitatively [12:3.12]. This circuit is exclusive to the Father, but he is not excluded from the other circuits; being infinite, he acts over all four absolute-gravity circuits [12:3.1].

5. What This Means for Our Faith

The fact that the personality circuit is exclusive to the Father means that every personality is held directly by the Father. The book says that the Father's love individualizes each personality as "⟦Q 12:7.9⟧a child without duplicate in infinity⟦/Q⟧" [12:7.9], and it comforts us: "⟦Q 12:7.12⟧the Father is not very far from any one of you⟦/Q⟧" [12:7.12]. As physical gravity holds the stars, so personality gravity, in a way that cannot be measured, is drawing us to the Father.

Summary

The four absolute gravity circuits are the personality gravity of the Father, the spirit gravity of the Son, the mind gravity of the Conjoint Actor, and the physical gravity of Paradise, and all are absolute presence circuits independent of time and space [12:3.2-6]. Physical gravity acts mostly beyond the organized universes [12:3.8], spirit gravity functions almost wholly in the grand universe [12:3.9], and about eighty-five per cent of mind gravity originates in the grand universe [12:3.10]. Personality gravity alone is the Father's circuit, which cannot be measured [12:3.12].

q168.question: What does the teaching of "the part and the whole" mean, that the will of God does not necessarily prevail in one person's heart but does rule the universe as a whole?
q168.answer:
The Urantia Book says: "⟦Q 12:7.1⟧Mercy characterizes God's attitude of love for the individual; impartiality motivates God's attitude toward the total⟦/Q⟧" [12:7.1]. And it explains that the will of God does not necessarily prevail in the part, the heart of any one personality, but does rule the whole, the universe of universes [12:7.1]. This means that God does not force individuals who possess free will, but the direction of the whole universe is firmly maintained within his will.

This teaching can be understood from three aspects: the laws of God and freedom, the individual and the community, and the growth of faith in time.

1. The Laws of God Are Not Arbitrary

Throughout all time and space there is operative an impersonal law equivalent to the function of a cosmic providence [12:7.1]. To our limited vision the acts of God may appear dictatorial and arbitrary, but "⟦Q 12:7.2⟧The laws of God are merely the habits of God⟦/Q⟧" [12:7.2], simply his best way of repeatedly doing things. The book also asks us to remember that nature is not the exclusive act of Deity; other influences are present in those phenomena which man calls nature [12:7.2].

2. God Is Not a Slave to Law

God is not a self-acting automatic force or a law-bound power; "⟦Q 12:7.6⟧He is a freewill and primal personality⟦/Q⟧" [12:7.6]. Thus, if a better way is called for in a certain situation, God functions in that way, and this is not the overriding of a lower law but the expression of a higher law [12:7.3]. Because he is changeless, we can depend on him to act in the same way in ordinary situations, and he is the guarantee of the stability of all created things and beings [12:7.5].

3. The Longer the Time, the More the Will of God Is Revealed

The will of God does not uniformly prevail in the heart of the God-seeking mortal, but as the time frame is enlarged from a single moment to the whole of the first life, the will of God becomes increasingly discernible in the spirit fruits borne in the lives of the spirit-led [12:7.7]. And as it is further enlarged to include morontia experience, that will shines ever more brightly [12:7.7]. This is an encouragement not to lose heart over today's failures but to look at the whole of the long ascending journey.

4. Fatherhood and Brotherhood: The Paradox of the Part and the Whole

"⟦Q 12:7.8⟧The Fatherhood of God and the brotherhood of man present the paradox of the part and the whole on the level of personality⟦/Q⟧" [12:7.8]. God loves each person as an individual child in the heavenly family, yet he so loves every individual, and the universality of his love brings into being the universal brotherhood [12:7.8, 12:7.10]. The Father's love absolutely individualizes each personality as a will creature irreplaceable in all eternity [12:7.9].

5. My Good Deeds and My Errors Affect Everyone

Since brotherhood is a fact of relationship between every personality in universal existence, no person can escape the benefits or the penalties that come from relationship to other persons [12:7.11]. "⟦Q 12:7.11⟧The good effort of each man benefits all men; the error or evil of each man augments the tribulation of all men⟦/Q⟧" [12:7.11]. As moves the part, so moves the whole; and as the progress of the whole, so the progress of the part [12:7.11]. Therefore an individual's life of faith never remains a merely private matter.

6. The Father Who Is Far Away and Yet Nearest of All

It is a mystery that God has his residential headquarters on Paradise and at the same time is personally in contact with a well-nigh infinite number of beings in a vast universe, but this should not weaken our faith [12:7.12]. The Father dwells within you, and the fragment of the Father in the mortal mind holds mysterious communion with the human soul [12:7.12-13].

Summary

God deals with the individual in mercy and with the whole in impartiality [12:7.1]. His will does not always prevail in the heart of a single person endowed with free will, but it rules the whole universe and is revealed ever more clearly over the long time of ascension [12:7.1, 12:7.7]. Because God loves each person uniquely, all become brothers [12:7.9-10], and so one person's goodness and errors affect the whole [12:7.11].

q169.question: What is each of the Father's seven sacred worlds that circle Paradise like, and why are so many secrets kept there?
q169.answer:
Between Paradise and Havona the satellite spheres of Paradise circle in three circuits, and the innermost of these circuits is the Father's seven sacred worlds [13:1.1]. These worlds contain "⟦Q 13:1.1⟧the only inherent personality secrets in the universe of universes⟦/Q⟧" [13:1.1], and they are directed by the Trinitized Secrets of Supremacy, the highest order of the Stationary Sons of the Trinity [13:1.2].

One reason these worlds are secret is that each sphere enjoys a specialized expression of the Deities composing the Paradise Trinity, a unique presence of divinity that can be recognized and understood only by the particular groups who reside on it or are admitted to it [13:1.3].

1. The Seven Worlds and Their Secrets

Divinington: the "⟦Q 13:1.4⟧bosom of the Father⟦/Q⟧" and the Paradise rendezvous of the Thought Adjusters. The bestowal and mission of the Adjusters, their nature and origin, and their technique of contact with human beings are the secrets of this world [13:1.4-5].

Sonarington: the "⟦Q 13:1.7⟧bosom of the Son⟦/Q⟧" and the Paradise headquarters of the descending and ascending Sons of God. The incarnation of the divine Sons is its secret [13:1.7-8].

Spiritington: the "⟦Q 13:1.9⟧bosom of the Spirit⟦/Q⟧," where the Seven Master Spirits and certain of their offspring forgather; the mysteries of reflectivity are its secret [13:1.9-10].

Vicegerington: the "⟦Q 13:1.11⟧bosom of the Father and the Son⟦/Q⟧," which keeps the secrets of trinitization, that is, the secrets of the authority to represent the Trinity [13:1.11-12].

Solitarington: the "⟦Q 13:1.15⟧bosom of the Father and the Spirit⟦/Q⟧," the home of the Solitary Messengers, and in the present universe age also the status sphere of the Universe Power Directors [13:1.15-16].

Seraphington: the "⟦Q 13:1.19⟧bosom of the Son and the Spirit⟦/Q⟧," the destiny sphere of all ministering orders of the angelic hosts, which keeps the mysteries of seraphic transport [13:1.19-20].

Ascendington: the "⟦Q 13:1.21⟧bosom of the Father, Son, and Spirit⟦/Q⟧," the rendezvous of the ascendant creatures, which keeps the mystery of the evolution of the immortal soul within the mortal mind [13:1.21-22].

2. Secrets Are Not Discrimination but the Protection of Trust

The revelator says that if the truths of Divinington were revealed, they would rather confuse him in his work, and might even exceed the conceptual capacity of his order of being [13:1.6]. And "⟦Q 13:2.8⟧When the Creator has an experiential personality secret with his creature, the Creator preserves that secret in eternal confidence⟦/Q⟧" [13:2.8]. Secrets, in other words, are a way of respecting the unique experience of each order of beings.

3. Doors That Open to Mortals and Doors That Stay Closed

When mortals reach Havona they are granted admission to Ascendington, and after being mustered into the Corps of the Finality they may also enter Sonarington, but the one-seventh sector reserved for the secrets of incarnation will not be opened to them [13:2.6]. Eventually they will have relative access to the other spheres except Divinington, but they will never land on the shores of Divinington [13:2.7]. Yet the book adds that we shall surely stand repeatedly at the "⟦Q 13:2.7⟧right hand of the Father⟦/Q⟧" [13:2.7].

4. A Secret Belonging Only to Humans: Ascendington

Interestingly, one seventh of Ascendington is forbidden to the revelator, a high being of Trinity origin, because that sector holds the secret of an experience belonging only to beings of the human type, the fusion of the Adjuster with the human soul [13:1.23]. Even after it is revealed to us, that secret will remain our secret forever [13:1.23]. Ascendington will always be our home address, even when we serve in outer space, and it will be the home of our sentimental memories [13:2.1].

Summary

The Father's seven worlds are the "bosoms" and rendezvous of the Deities and of various orders of beings, and each keeps its own secrets, such as those of the Adjusters, of incarnation, of reflectivity, and of trinitization [13:1.4-22]. These secrets are an expression of trust that respects the experience of each order [13:2.8], and to mortals too is entrusted a secret known only to themselves, the mystery of the evolution of the immortal soul [13:1.22-23].

q170.question: Why does the eternal central universe of Havona exist, and what is life on Havona like?
q170.answer:
Havona is the eternal and perfect central universe surrounding Paradise. The Urantia Book broadly divides the activities of Havona into Havonal, Paradisiacal, and ascendant-finite activities [14:6.1-4], and explains that this perfect creation serves in different ways seven orders of universe intelligence, from the Deities to the ascending mortals [14:6.5]. At the same time the revelator adds that the central universe probably also contributes to many purposes that have not been revealed to him [14:6.5].

In a word, Havona is the joy of perfection to the Deities, the pattern for the evolutionary universes, and the gateway into Paradise for the ascenders.

1. What Havona Means to the Deities

God the Father derives supreme parental satisfaction from the perfection of Havona, and "⟦Q 14:6.6⟧The perfect Creator is divinely pleased with the adoration of the perfect creature⟦/Q⟧" [14:6.6]. The realization of perfection in Havona compensates for the time-space delay in the urge of infinite expansion [14:6.7]. To the Eternal Son, Havona is the first and eternally final demonstration that the Son is the Word of the Father [14:6.15], and to the Infinite Spirit it was the stage of rehearsal for the ministry of mercy in the evolutionary universes [14:6.18]. Havona is also the eternal and perfect proof of the spiritual reality of the Supreme Being and foreshadows the future unification of the Supreme [14:6.23-24].

2. A Pattern and Training Ground for the Evolutionary Universes

Havona is the educational training ground in which the Creator Sons prepare for their adventures in universe creation, and a Creator Son strives that his universe may eventually attain this Paradise-Havona level of perfection [14:6.27]. The Universe Mother Spirits also receive their prepersonal training on the worlds of Havona [14:6.32]. The Havona worlds are the "mind laboratory" [14:6.20] that serves as the pattern for all creature minds, and they are the postgraduate school of mind for all beings destined to Paradise [14:6.21].

3. For Ascending Mortals Havona Is the Gateway

Havona is the pre-Paradise training goal of all ascending mortals, and here mortals attain the Supreme Being, the pre-Paradise Deity [14:6.38]. The book says, "⟦Q 14:6.39⟧Paradise is the home, and Havona the workshop and playground, of the finaliters⟦/Q⟧" [14:6.39]. Beginning on the seventh circuit, the ascenders progress toward the inner circuits, attaining in turn the Master Spirit, the Supreme, the Infinite Spirit, the Eternal Son, and the Universal Father [14:5.4]. Interestingly, the name "circles of progress" in the human mind is said to derive from this arrangement of Havona [14:5.4].

4. Life on Havona: A World without Monotony

Life on Havona is so rich and full that it transcends the human concept of anything a created being could experience, and even the technique of thinking differs from that of Urantia [14:5.2]. Its regulations are not arbitrary but natural, so that the ascender comes naturally to enjoy doing things in the way they ought to be done [14:5.3]. Each of the billion worlds is an original and unique creation [14:5.6], and "⟦Q 14:5.9⟧Monotony is not a part of the Havona career⟦/Q⟧" [14:5.9].

5. The Lesson for Us Now

The book says that the love of adventure, curiosity, and the dread of monotony were not given to torment us, but to suggest that death is only the beginning of an endless career of adventure [14:5.10]. These urges are often repressed and disappointed on earth, but during the long ages to come they will be fully realized and gloriously gratified [14:5.11].

Summary

Havona gives the Deities the satisfaction of perfection, serves the Creator Sons and Mother Spirits as pattern and training ground, and is for all ascenders the gateway in which they attain the Supreme Being and enter Paradise [14:6.6, 14:6.27, 14:6.38]. Life there is full of endless surprises [14:5.9], and our curiosity and love of adventure are divine endowments given for that very eternal journey [14:5.10-11].

q171.question: How is the superuniverse government headed by the Ancients of Days organized and operated?
q171.answer:
The superuniverse headquarters is the seat of the high spiritual government of the time-space domains, and each superuniverse is presided over by three Ancients of Days, the joint supreme executives [15:10.1, 15:10.3]. The headquarters of our superuniverse, Orvonton, is Uversa. The superuniverse government has a unique structure in which an executive branch originating in the realms of perfection works together with a deliberative branch that has risen from the evolutionary universes [15:11.1].

1. Who Are the Ancients of Days?

The Ancients of Days are Supreme Trinity Personalities, all basically identical, and they disclose the combined character of the Trinity [18:3.2]. Whereas the Seven Master Spirits determine the nature of each superuniverse, the Ancients of Days dictate its administration, insuring uniformity of administration and the harmony of the whole among the seven differing superuniverses [18:3.3]. They were all trinitized at the same time, and the trinitization of these twenty-one beings is said to be the first record in the personality records of Paradise [18:3.4]. They always rule as a group of three [18:3.5].

2. The Seven Groups of the Executive Branch

The executive branch of the superuniverse government is composed of seven groups: the Ancients of Days, the Perfectors of Wisdom, the Divine Counselors, the Universal Censors, the Mighty Messengers, Those High in Authority, and Those without Name and Number [15:10.3-10]. The first three groups are co-ordinate Trinity personalities of direct origin in the Paradise Trinity [15:10.11]. The last three groups are glorified ascendant mortals who, after being mustered into the Corps of the Finality, were embraced by the Trinity and assigned to the service of the Ancients of Days [15:10.12]. "⟦Q 15:10.12⟧Thus was the executive branch of the superuniverse government enlarged to include the glorified and perfected children of the evolutionary worlds⟦/Q⟧" [15:10.12].

3. The Deliberative Assembly: The Democracy of Evolution

The legislative or advisory council of the superuniverse consists of seven assemblies, and each local universe admitted to membership elects one native representative to each assembly [15:11.2]. These representatives are chosen from among the graduates of the Orvonton ascendant pilgrimage who are tarrying on Uversa, accredited for transport to Havona [15:11.2]. The revelator says he knows of no disagreement between the Orvonton executives and the Uversa assembly, and that this testifies that evolutionary beings can truly attain the heights of perfected wisdom [15:11.3].

4. The Supreme Tribunals: A Judiciary without Separate Personnel

The superuniverse has a judicial branch, but it has no separate personnel [15:12.1]. Depending on the case, an Ancient of Days, a Perfector of Wisdom, or a Divine Counselor presides; the Censors present the evidence, the Mighty Messengers defend the children of time, and Those High in Authority voice the attitude of the higher government [15:12.1]. The Sons of the local universes can decree the survival of mortal man, "⟦Q 15:12.2⟧but only the Ancients of Days may sit in executive judgment on the issues of eternal life and death⟦/Q⟧" [15:12.2]. There is no appeal from their verdicts [15:12.4].

5. The Sector Governments and the Trinity Regime

The major sectors, each about one tenth of a superuniverse, are administered by the Perfections of Days, and the minor sectors, each containing about one billion inhabitable worlds, by the Recents of Days [15:13.1, 15:13.4]. The reports of the Unions of Days stationed in the local universes and of the Faithfuls of Days attached to the constellations go up through the minor and major sectors to the courts of the Ancients of Days [15:13.6]. The superuniverses, however, are wholly isolated from one another and know of each other's affairs only through the Paradise clearinghouse [15:10.23].

6. The Shape of the Future

Because the ruling prerogatives of the Ancients of Days were not acquired by experience, they will someday be superseded by the Supreme Being, the experiential sovereign, and will become his vicegerents [18:3.8]. In the present age, while the evolution of the Supreme is incomplete, they are providing a co-ordinated and perfect administrative overcontrol [18:3.9].

Summary

The superuniverse government consists of an executive branch of seven groups headed by the Ancients of Days, a deliberative assembly made up of ascendant graduates, and supreme tribunals that operate without separate personnel [15:10.3-10, 15:11.2, 15:12.1]. The final verdicts concerning eternal life and death are entrusted to them alone [15:12.2, 18:3.7], and this government is the place where perfection and evolution meet face to face and co-operate [15:11.1].

q172.question: What is "virtue" as The Urantia Book speaks of it, and how does man's moral nature differ from animal intelligence?
q172.answer:
The Urantia Book says, "⟦Q 16:7.1⟧Intelligence alone cannot explain the moral nature⟦/Q⟧" [16:7.1]. Morality, virtue, is indigenous to human personality, and moral intuition, the realization of duty, is a component of human mind endowment, together with scientific curiosity and spiritual insight [16:7.1]. What especially distinguishes man from the animal world is not the degree of his intelligence but his moral and religious natures [16:7.1].

And virtue is defined as "⟦Q 16:7.6⟧righteousness—conformity with the cosmos⟦/Q⟧" [16:7.6]. Virtue is known not by naming it but by living it, and it is realized in daily life by consistently choosing good rather than evil [16:7.6].

1. The Animal Learns by Leaping, the Personality by Looking

The selective responses of animals are limited to the motor level of behavior, and the insight of the higher animals ordinarily appears only after motor trial and error [16:7.2]. Man, by contrast, can exercise scientific, moral, and spiritual insight prior to all exploration or experimentation [16:7.2]. "⟦Q 16:7.3⟧A personality can look before it leaps⟦/Q⟧" [16:7.3], and therefore learns not only from leaping but also from looking.

2. Discriminating Not Only Means but Ends

An animal, as experience accumulates, can choose one among several ways of reaching a goal. But a personality can examine the goal itself and judge its worth [16:7.4]. Intelligence alone merely seeks the best means of attaining indiscriminate ends, whereas a moral being discriminates not only between means but also between ends [16:7.4]. Thus one who chooses virtue knows what he is doing and why, where he is going and how he will get there [16:7.4]. Conversely, when a man fails to discriminate the ends of his striving, he functions on the animal level of existence [16:7.5].

3. Virtue Requires the Art of Measurement

The choice between good and evil is influenced not only by the keenness of the moral nature but also by ignorance, immaturity, and delusion [16:7.7]. Because evil may be committed when, through distortion or deception, the lesser is chosen in place of the greater, a sense of proportion and the art of relative evaluation enter into the exercise of virtue [16:7.7]. Without the art of measurement that discerns meanings with precision, the moral nature would be impotent, and without the cosmic insight that brings consciousness of spiritual values, moral choice would be futile [16:7.8].

4. Morality Spreads Not by Compulsion but by Contagion

"⟦Q 16:7.9⟧Morality can never be advanced by law or by force⟦/Q⟧" [16:7.9]. It is a personal and freewill matter and must be disseminated by "contagion," through the contact of morally fragrant persons with those who are in some measure desirous of doing the Father's will [16:7.9]. Here lies the reason why a community of faith should value the example of life more than rules.

5. Supreme Virtue

Moral acts are performances of the highest intelligence, guided by discrimination in the choice of superior ends and in the selection of moral means to attain those ends [16:7.10]. Thus the book concludes: "⟦Q 16:7.10⟧Supreme virtue, then, is wholeheartedly to choose to do the will of the Father in heaven⟦/Q⟧" [16:7.10]. The explanation that the relative free will of human personality is concerned with moral decisions and with wholehearted devotion to doing the Father's will is in the same vein [16:8.7-8, 16:8.13].

Summary

Virtue is righteousness, conformity with the cosmos, and it is realized in a life that consistently chooses the good [16:7.6]. The animal learns means through trial and error, but the personality has insight in advance of experience and discerns the value of the ends themselves [16:7.3-4]. Morality spreads not by compulsion but by the contagion of fragrant lives [16:7.9], and its summit is wholeheartedly choosing to do the will of the Father [16:7.10].

q173.question: What does "cosmic discrimination" mean, by which the cosmic mind responds on the three levels of causation, duty, and worship?
q173.answer:
According to The Urantia Book, the Seven Master Spirits are the sevenfold source of the cosmic mind, and the cosmic mind is a subabsolute manifestation of the mind of the Third Source and Center [16:6.1]. Urantians live under the influence of the Creative Spirit of Nebadon rather than the direct influence of the Seven Master Spirits, yet the Master Spirits still dominate the basic reactions of all creature mind [16:6.2]. The ability of this cosmic mind to respond unerringly on three levels of reality, namely causation, duty, and worship, is what the book calls "cosmic discrimination" [16:6.5-8].

Because of this endowment, man is not the helpless victim of the implicit a priori assumptions of science, philosophy, and religion [16:6.4].

1. Reality Response: The Ability of Mind to Respond to Reality

All personality associations of the cosmic mind have a quality that might be called the "reality response" [16:6.4]. Just as energy-matter responds to gravity, the reality sensitivity of the cosmic mind responds to certain phases of reality [16:6.4]. The fact of the cosmic mind also explains the kinship of various types of minds, and this is why human minds sometimes move in channels of agreement that cannot be explained [16:6.3].

2. The Three Cosmic Discriminations

Causation: the reality domain of the physical senses, the scientific realm of logical uniformity, and "⟦Q 16:6.6⟧the mathematical form of the cosmic discrimination⟦/Q⟧" [16:6.6].

Duty: the reality domain of morals in the philosophic realm, the recognition of relative right and wrong; this is the judicial form of the cosmic discrimination [16:6.7].

Worship: the spiritual domain of religious experience, the personal realization of divine fellowship, the assurance of eternal survival. This is "⟦Q 16:6.8⟧the highest insight of the cosmic mind⟦/Q⟧" [16:6.8], the worshipful form of the cosmic discrimination.

3. The Starting Point of Science, Philosophy, and Religion

These three insights are the a priori assumptions that enable man to function as a rational and self-conscious personality in the realms of science, philosophy, and religion [16:6.10]. Matter-energy is recognized by the mathematical logic of the senses; mind-reason intuitively knows its moral duty; spirit-faith recognizes the reality of spiritual experience [16:6.10]. And it is these three cosmic intuitions that give objective validity to human experience of things, meanings, and values [16:6.10]. In the description of Urantia personality, too, the three recognitions of the uniformity of causation, moral duty, and fellowship worship of Deity appear again [16:8.15-18].

4. When Unified, They Make for Strong Character

These three factors may be unified in personality development or may become unbalanced in relation to one another. But when unified, they produce a strong character consisting of a correlation of factual science, moral philosophy, and genuine religious experience [16:6.10]. The book laments that too few persons on Urantia take delight in cultivating the qualities of courageous and independent cosmic thinking [16:6.9].

5. The Purpose of Education, Civilization, and Religion

The book says that it is the purpose of education to develop these endowments, of civilization to express them, of life experience to realize them, "⟦Q 16:6.11⟧of religion to ennoble them; and of personality to unify them⟦/Q⟧" [16:6.11]. The believer should not fear science or regard morality merely as law, but should cultivate the three insights together and so achieve a balanced personality.

Summary

Cosmic discrimination is the threefold recognition of reality possessed by every will creature endowed with the cosmic mind: causation (science), duty (morality), and worship (religion) [16:6.5-9]. It is the a priori foundation of science, philosophy, and religion, and gives objective validity to experience [16:6.10]. When the three are unified, strong character results, and to unify them is the purpose of personality [16:6.10-11].

q174.question: What is "reflectivity," by which the superuniverse headquarters instantly knows what happens in the universe, and who are Majeston and the Reflective Spirits?
q174.answer:
Reflectivity is a marvelous universe phenomenon by which the superuniverse headquarters knows the important happenings within that superuniverse and transmits information upward to the central universe and downward to the local universes [15:10.2]. The Urantia Book says that reflectivity is a phenomenon of the mind levels of the Conjoint Actor, the Supreme Being, and the Master Spirits, and that it is transmissible to the beings concerned in its working [17:3.3]. Yet even the revelators do not fully understand its basic details, and reflectivity is kept on Spiritington as "⟦Q 13:1.10⟧a secret of God the Spirit⟦/Q⟧" [13:1.10].

1. Majeston: The Chief of Reflectivity

When all forty-nine Reflective Spirits had personalized and the cycle of reflective creation was complete, a new and far-reaching reaction occurred in the Deity Absolute, and Majeston, the reflectivity chief, was personalized [17:2.2]. The creation of Majeston was the first supreme creative act of the Supreme Being; the reaction of the Deity Absolute had not been foreseen and far exceeded the intent [17:2.5]. He is a true individual, maintaining Paradise headquarters at the rendezvous of the Seven Master Spirits, and is wholly devoted to the co-ordination and maintenance of the reflectivity service [17:2.3]. Since he is the only personality of divinity created by the Supreme Being in liaison with the Deity Absolute, he is not included in the Paradise personality roll [17:2.4].

2. The Reflective Spirits: Beings Who Reflect the Seven Divine Combinations

The Reflective Spirits are of Trinity origin, forty-nine in all. They were created seven at a time, by the Paradise Trinity in liaison with one of the Seven Master Spirits [17:2.1]. They therefore variously reflect the natures of the seven possible combinations of the divine association of Father, Son, and Spirit, and one of each of the seven types is stationed on each superuniverse headquarters so as to reflect perfectly all manifestations of the three Deities [17:3.1]. The Reflective Spirits of each superuniverse create the Reflective Image Aids, who become their personal voices in the courts of the Ancients of Days [17:3.4].

3. A Living System of Records and News

The Reflective Spirits are not mere transmitting agents but retentive personalities, and everything of true spiritual value is registered in duplicate [17:3.5]. The formal records of the universe are passed up through the angelic recorders, but the true spiritual records are assembled by reflectivity and preserved in the living minds of the family of the Infinite Spirit; "⟦Q 17:3.6⟧These are the live records⟦/Q⟧" [17:3.6]. The reflectivity organization also functions continually as the mechanism for gathering news and promulgating decrees [17:3.7].

4. A Personal, Not Automatic, Operation

Everything of importance that happens at a local universe headquarters is reflected to the superuniverse capital, and conversely, matters of superuniverse importance are reflected to the local universe capitals [17:3.8]. Though it appears to be automatic, it is in reality highly personal and intelligent, and its precision results from the perfection of personality co-operation [17:3.8]. Thus the Ancients of Days need not personally leave their worlds, for those worlds are the superuniverse focal points of the far-flung reflectivity system [18:3.5].

5. Range and Mystery

In the present universe age the range of the reflectivity service appears to be limited to the periphery of the seven superuniverses, but otherwise it seems to be independent of time and space [17:3.10]. Thought Adjusters do not participate in the operation of this system, but there is reason to believe that they are fully cognizant of its transactions and able to avail themselves of them [17:3.9]. Interestingly, neither the Master Spirits nor the Deities themselves directly disclose such powers of reflectivity, yet they created beings who possess them, and the book says: "⟦Q 17:3.3⟧Divine heredity does sometimes disclose in the creature certain attributes which are not discernible in the Creator⟦/Q⟧" [17:3.3].

Summary

Reflectivity is the system by which the superuniverse headquarters knows and transmits the important happenings of the universes above and below and preserves spiritual values as living records [15:10.2, 17:3.5-7]. At its center is Majeston, personalized by the first creative act of the Supreme Being [17:2.2-5], and the forty-nine Reflective Spirits and their aids carry on this work in each superuniverse [17:3.1, 17:3.4]. It is not an automatic device but the result of personal co-operation [17:3.8], and it remains a secret of God the Spirit [13:1.10].

q175.question: What kind of beings are the "Inspired Trinity Spirits," said to be wholly secret, and how are they related to human beings?
q175.answer:
The Inspired Trinity Spirits are one of the few orders of wholly secret beings that have come into existence by the act of the Paradise Trinity [19:5.1]. Even the revelator of Trinity origin who wrote this account confesses that he does not fully understand their nature and conduct, and says that they probably belong to the category of superpersonal spirits [19:5.2]. In a word the book calls them "⟦Q 19:5.3⟧a secret of the Paradise Trinity⟦/Q⟧" [19:5.3].

Nevertheless, the book offers an interesting inference that their activities may not be unrelated to the spiritual growth of us human beings.

1. Origin and Nature

They come into existence by the act of the Trinity, and they may be utilized by one, two, or all three of the Deities [19:5.1]. It is not known whether their number is complete or increasing, but the revelator believes it is not fixed [19:5.1]. They function through all known circuits and appear to act almost independently of time and space [19:5.2].
