They are not a part of the revealed organization that conducts the time-space universes before light and life, and they have no clearly discernible place in the administration of the superuniverses [19:5.3].

2. Who Can Recognize Them?

Under certain conditions they can individualize themselves sufficiently to be recognized by beings of Trinity origin, but the lower orders of celestial beings can never recognize them [19:5.3]. Much of what is known about them comes from the Solitary Messengers, who detect the nearness of these Spirits as the magnetic needle points to the magnetic pole [19:5.5]. The revelator writes that even at the moment of writing, an associate Solitary Messenger informs him that a Spirit of this order is present with them, within twenty-five feet [19:5.7].

3. A Possible Connection with Thought Adjusters

When a Solitary Messenger is on a planet whose inhabitants are indwelt by Thought Adjusters, as on Urantia, a qualitative excitation occurs in his sensitivity of spirit-presence detection [19:5.6]. In contact with the natives of planets that do not receive Adjusters there is no such response. This suggests that the Thought Adjusters are in some way associated with the Inspired Spirits, but the revelator says he does not really know [19:5.6]. Since Adjusters originate in the Father alone and Inspired Spirits in the Trinity, the two are not of the same order [19:5.6].

4. Possibly Superconscious Teachers

The revelator's most interesting conclusion is this: just as the Trinity Teacher Sons are devoted to the conscious enlightenment of universe creatures, the Inspired Trinity Spirits, "⟦Q 19:5.9⟧by superconscious techniques, are also functioning as teachers of the realms⟦/Q⟧" [19:5.9]. There is a body of spiritual knowledge essential to high spiritual attainment that cannot be consciously received, and self-consciousness might actually jeopardize its reception [19:5.9]. The Sons of God, too, are not conscious of the counsel of the Inspired Spirits, yet they tell of happenings that are difficult to explain without taking the activity of such Spirits into account [19:5.10].

5. Their Future Role

The Melchizedeks of Nebadon teach that the Inspired Trinity Spirits are destined, in the eternal future, to function in the place of the Solitary Messengers, whose number is slowly diminishing [19:5.4].

6. The Lesson for Us

The revelator says he does not believe they are playing hide and seek, and that he is satisfied "⟦Q 19:5.11⟧that there are no arbitrary secrets in the universe⟦/Q⟧" [19:5.11]. And he counsels that we mortals have a long way to go before we can depend on the assurance of sight, so that for a long time we shall make use of faith and depend on revelation if we are to progress rapidly and safely [19:5.12]. Not being conscious of unseen help does not mean that the help is absent.

Summary

The Inspired Trinity Spirits are superpersonal and wholly secret spirits of Trinity origin, whose presence only the Solitary Messengers can sense [19:5.1-5]. They may have a special connection with worlds indwelt by Adjusters [19:5.6], and they may be teachers who superconsciously impart spiritual truth that cannot be received consciously [19:5.9]. This mystery reminds us that we must advance relying on faith and revelation rather than on what is seen [19:5.12].

q176.question: How is the mortal bestowal of an Avonal Son like, and how is it unlike, the bestowal of a Michael (a Creator Son)?
q176.answer:
The Urantia Book says: "⟦Q 20:6.5⟧The mortal-bestowal careers of the Michaels and the Avonals, while comparable in most respects, are not identical in all⟦/Q⟧" [20:6.5]. Both Sons are born of woman, grow up as human beings, pass through death, and open the way for the outpouring of the Spirit of Truth. But the will that is the source of the bestowal, the number and form of the bestowals, and their meaning within the universe differ.

It should first be made clear that the purpose of a bestowal is not to change the attitude of the Father. The bestowals of the Avonals and the Michaels are an essential part of the experiential training that makes these Sons safe and sympathetic magistrates and rulers of the peoples of time and space [20:5.2].

1. The Likeness: A Truly Human Life

On a mortal-bestowal mission a Paradise Son is always born of woman, grows up through infancy and youth to manhood, and becomes in every way like the human beings of his race [20:6.2]. There is, however, the universal restriction that he does not leave offspring on the bestowal world [20:6.2]. He toils in various callings [20:6.3], and after achieving perfect harmony with the indwelling Thought Adjuster, he begins his mission as a teacher who awakens the minds of his brethren [20:6.4]. Both, upon entering the portals of death, reappear on the third day [20:6.6].

2. The Difference: By Whose Will He Comes

Michael on Urantia proclaimed that whoever has seen the Son has seen the Father, but an Avonal never so proclaims. Instead, he declares: "⟦Q 20:6.5⟧Whosoever has seen me has seen the Eternal Son of God⟦/Q⟧" [20:6.5]. The Avonals are not of immediate descent from the Father and do not incarnate subject to the Father's will; always do they bestow themselves subject to the will of the Eternal Son [20:6.5].

3. The Difference: Once and Seven Times

An Avonal bestowal is always in the likeness of mortal flesh, whereas the seven bestowals of a Creator Son include appearing on seven creature levels of being [21:4.2]. Only once in his sevenfold bestowal career is a Michael born of woman, and only once does he live and die as a member of the lowest order of evolutionary will creatures [21:4.3]. Most inhabited worlds receive an Avonal bestowal Son; the one exception is the single planet chosen by the Creator Son for his mortal bestowal [20:5.4].

4. Their Effectiveness Is Not Different

Of the planetary services of the Avonals the book emphasizes: "⟦Q 20:5.6⟧in no way are these planetary services inferior to the mortal bestowals of the Michaels⟦/Q⟧" [20:5.6]. No planet could ever be in such a condition that it would require the bestowal of a Creator Son for its spiritual rehabilitation; any Son of the bestowal group would have equally sufficed [20:5.6]. Moreover, there is no record of failure by an Avonal or a Michael on a bestowal mission [20:5.7].

5. Death and the Spirit of Truth

A bestowal Son must encounter death, but it is not a requirement of the divine plan that this death be violent [20:6.6]. Most planets afford a more considerate reception, and Urantia, because of the unusually cruel experience through which Jesus passed, has become known as "⟦Q 20:6.6⟧the world of the cross⟦/Q⟧" [20:6.6]. A bestowal Son lays down his life voluntarily, not to appease stern justice or divine wrath, but to complete his bestowal [20:6.7]. After an Avonal bestowal, the conjoint Spirit of Truth of that Son and the Creator Son is sent [20:6.8], and when the final bestowal of a Michael is completed, that Spirit becomes more literally the spirit of the sovereign Michael [20:6.9]. It is also after the outpouring of this Spirit of Truth that Adjusters come to all normal human beings [20:5.3].

Summary

Avonals and Michaels are both born, live, and die as true human beings, and they open the way of the Spirit of Truth [20:6.2, 20:6.6, 20:6.8]. But an Avonal bestows himself once by the will of the Eternal Son and reveals the Eternal Son, whereas a Michael bestows himself on seven creature levels and at last reveals the Father [20:6.5, 21:4.2-3]. Their effectiveness is not different [20:5.6], and Urantia receives special attention because it was the stage of Michael's final bestowal [20:5.5].

q177.question: When a Creator Son creates a local universe, what can he make by himself, and in what matters does he need the consent or co-operation of the other Deities?
q177.answer:
A Creator Son is the designer, creator, builder, and administrator of a local universe [21:2.1]. He leaves Paradise and becomes the head of his universe, to all practical purposes its God [21:2.2], but his creative prerogatives are not unlimited. The Urantia Book explains that his departure liberates his creator prerogatives from the Paradise sources, yet he remains subject to certain limitations inherent in the pre-existence of those sources [21:2.3].

1. A Long Preparation before Creation

A Creator Son may choose the space site of his universe, but before beginning its physical organization he must spend a long period of observation, studying the efforts of his older brothers who created universes earlier in the same superuniverse [21:2.1]. Before this he completes the long and unique experience of Paradise observation and Havona training [21:2.1]. The Creator Son is accompanied by a creative daughter of the Infinite Spirit, the one who is to become the divine minister, the Mother Spirit, of the new local universe [21:2.2].

2. Three Limitations of Creative Prerogative

Energy-matter: this is dominated by the Infinite Spirit. Before a Creator Son can create any new form of things or attempt any new transmutation of energy-matter, he must secure the consent and working co-operation of the Infinite Spirit [21:2.4].

Creature designs and types: these are controlled by the Eternal Son. Before making any new type of being or new design of creature, the Creator Son must secure the consent of the Eternal Son [21:2.5].

Personality: "⟦Q 21:2.6⟧Personality is designed and bestowed by the Universal Father⟦/Q⟧" [21:2.6]. The Creator Son cannot bestow personality by himself.

Furthermore, the types and patterns of mind are determined by precreature factors, and after a creature has been constituted, mind is bestowed by the Third Source and Center [21:2.7]. Spirit design is finally controlled by the spirit endowment of the Trinity or of the Trinity personalities [21:2.8].

3. Co-creation with the Mother Spirit

When the problems of universe materialization and equilibrium have been settled and the Creator Son has formed a co-operative working union with the complemental Daughter of the Infinite Spirit, the two begin the liaison that gives origin to the numerous hosts of local universe children [21:2.9]. At this time the creative Spirit focalization of the Infinite Spirit changes in nature, taking on the personal qualities of the local universe Mother Spirit [21:2.9]. Thus the native beings of a local universe inherit half their attributes from the Creative Spirits, who are similar, and the other half from the Creator Sons, who differ from one another [21:2.10].

4. The Source of Diversity

All Creator Sons resemble their Paradise parents, yet none exactly resembles another; each is unique in both personality and nature [21:2.10]. Because of this diversity the life forms of the realms they found are also diverse, and no two realms are inhabited by native beings identical in every respect [21:2.10].

5. The Universe Goes On Even When the Son Is Absent

When a Creator Son is absent, the government is directed by the first-born native being, the Bright and Morning Star, and the Mother Spirit always remains at headquarters, carrying on her spiritual ministry [21:2.11]. Even when the Son lays down the lines of power in order to incarnate as a child of time, his realm continues to swing on, for no material organization is independent of the absolute gravity of Paradise and the overcontrol of the Unqualified Absolute [21:2.12]. This is also the background that made it possible for Michael to live as Jesus.

6. The Change after Sovereignty Is Attained

When he has completed his seven bestowals and attained supreme sovereignty, the power to create wholly new types of creatures in the present universe age passes from the Michael Son [21:5.6]. But the work of life elaboration already begun continues without interruption [21:5.6].

Summary

The Creator Son designs and builds the local universe, but in energy-matter he must have the consent and co-operation of the Infinite Spirit, and in creature design that of the Eternal Son, while personality is bestowed by the Universal Father alone [21:2.4-6]. Mind is bestowed by the Third Source, and spirit design is controlled by the Trinity [21:2.7-8]. He brings forth children together with the Mother Spirit [21:2.9], and because of his unique individuality, life is richly varied in each local universe [21:2.10].

q178.question: A Creator Son could have possessed full sovereignty from the beginning, so why does he earn his sovereignty "by experience" through seven bestowals?
q178.answer:
The Urantia Book says: "⟦Q 21:3.3⟧The fact of creatorship implies the fullness of sovereignty, but the Michaels choose to experientially earn it⟦/Q⟧" [21:3.3]. A Creator Son is at first given his universe with the consent of the Trinity and the confirmation of the Master Spirit, but this is only a kind of cosmic leasehold [21:3.1]. His elevation to the experiential supremacy of sovereignty comes as the result of the personal experience accumulated in the work of universe creation and incarnated bestowals [21:3.1]. Until then he rules as the vicegerent of the Universal Father [21:3.1].

1. Why He Does Not Assert Sovereignty in Advance

A Creator Son could at any time assert full sovereignty, but he wisely chooses not to [21:3.2]. If he were to assume unearned supreme sovereignty before passing through the bestowals, the Paradise personalities in his local universe would withdraw [21:3.2]. By earning sovereignty experientially, the Michaels retain the full co-operation of all Paradise personalities [21:3.3]. He swears to the Trinity that he will not assume supreme sovereignty until his seven bestowals are completed and certified by the superuniverse rulers, and such an oath would have no meaning if he did not have the power to do so [21:3.12]. This, in other words, is the voluntary humility of a freewill Son [21:3.3].

2. The Stages of Sovereignty

The book says that sovereignty passes through six, possibly seven, stages: initial vicegerent sovereignty, joint vicegerent sovereignty, augmenting vicegerent sovereignty, supreme sovereignty, increased supreme sovereignty, Trinitarian sovereignty, and unrevealed sovereignty [21:3.4-11]. In Nebadon, supreme sovereignty began with the end of Michael's Urantia bestowal and has existed for a little over nineteen hundred years [21:3.8].

3. The Content of the Seven Bestowals

The seven bestowals include appearing on seven creature levels of being and are related to the seven primary expressions of the will and nature of Deity [21:4.2]. Their technique includes experientially penetrating the seven levels in the very likeness of the creatures, dedicating himself to each phase of the sevenfold will of Deity as it is personalized in the Seven Master Spirits, and unifying these two experiences [21:3.17-22]. Their repercussions augment the sovereignty of the Supreme Being and factualize Michael's supreme local universe sovereignty [21:3.23]. After each bestowal he goes to the "⟦Q 21:4.4⟧right hand of the Father⟦/Q⟧" to gain acceptance [21:4.4].

4. Jesus' "It Is Finished"

The divine Son who appeared on Urantia was a Creator Son who had already completed six phases [21:4.5]. Therefore, when he gave up the life of the flesh, he could truly say "It is finished," and that death was the last step that completed his bestowal career [21:4.5]. From then on he rules no longer as a vicegerent but in his own right and name as "⟦Q 21:4.5⟧King of Kings and Lord of Lords⟦/Q⟧" [21:4.5].

5. A Way of Revealing the Nature of God

In the course of settling the question of sovereignty, the Creator Son not only demonstrates his fitness to rule but also reveals the nature of the Paradise Deities [21:3.24]. He humbles himself to take on the form and experience of the creature, and becomes the true revealer of the Father's loving nature and gracious authority [21:3.24]. A Creator who has completed his bestowals adds the experience of the creature to his nature and rises to the experiential plane of a "Master Son" [21:4.6].

6. A Comfort for Us

The book says that even the Gods must pass through an equivalent experience before they are accounted experientially competent to rule their universes fully; so "⟦Q 21:4.6⟧Why should man bemoan his lowly origin and enforced evolutionary career⟦/Q⟧" [21:4.6]! Growth through experience is the path that even the Sons of God walk.

Summary

A Creator Son could have asserted sovereignty from the beginning, but he chooses to earn it by experience through bestowals on seven creature levels [21:3.2-3, 21:4.2]. In this way he retains the co-operation of all Paradise personalities, reveals the sevenfold will and nature of Deity, and becomes a sympathetic ruler [21:3.3, 21:3.24]. Jesus' "It is finished" was the completion of this very seventh bestowal [21:4.5].

q179.question: What relationship does Michael, the Master Son who has completed his seven bestowals, have with his universe, and what is his future destiny?
q179.answer:
When a Creator Son completes his seven bestowals, he is reckoned as a separate order, a sevenfold Master Son [21:4.6]. The Urantia Book says that the power of a Master Michael is unlimited because it is derived from experienced association with the Trinity, and unquestioned because it is derived from actual experience as the very creatures subject to that authority [21:5.1]. Concerning his future, no one can speak with final authority, but the revelators infer that he will go on to service transcending the finite [21:6.1-2].

1. Three Reasons Why His Sovereignty Is Supreme

The sovereignty of a sevenfold Creator Son is supreme because it embraces the sevenfold viewpoint of Paradise Deity, because it embodies the sevenfold attitude of time-space creatures, and because it perfectly synthesizes the two [21:5.1-4]. This sovereignty therefore encompasses all the divinity of God the Sevenfold, culminating in the Supreme Being, and is like the future sovereignty of the Supreme Being that will someday be completed [21:5.5].

2. New Creation Ceases, and the Work of Nurture Begins

When supreme sovereignty is attained, the power to create wholly new types of creatures in the present universe age passes from Michael [21:5.6]. But the work of life elaboration already established continues without interruption, and the Master Son becomes responsible for personal devotion to the fostering and administering of what has already been created [21:5.6]. The book calls this the beginning of settled administration in a local universe [21:5.6].

3. The End of Confusion and the Triumph of Justice

The elevation of a Master Son means the beginning of the end of agelong uncertainty and confusion [21:5.7]. Thereafter, that which cannot be spiritualized will eventually be disorganized, and that which cannot be co-ordinated with cosmic reality will eventually be destroyed [21:5.7]. After endless mercy and patience have been fully extended, "⟦Q 21:5.7⟧That which mercy cannot rehabilitate justice will eventually annihilate⟦/Q⟧" [21:5.7].

4. A Ruler Supreme in His Own Universe

Once settled, the Master Michaels are supreme in authority, responsibility, and administrative power in their local universes, and there is no insight that surpasses their wisdom concerning the functioning of their universe [21:5.8]. He controls all other Sons of God in his domain and may modify the procedures of spiritual adjudication and evolutionary adjustment on the inhabited planets [21:5.9]. Especially with regard to the world of his creature sojourn and the planet of his incarnation in mortal flesh, he makes and carries out plans of his own choosing [21:5.9].

5. Intimate Contact through the Spirit of Truth

The Master Sons seem to be in perfect communication not only with the worlds of their own sojourn but with all worlds on which a Magisterial Son has bestowed himself, and this contact is maintained by their spiritual presence, the Spirit of Truth [21:5.10]. They possess "⟦Q 21:5.10⟧a sympathetic reach which extends from the Universal Father on high to the lowly races of planetary life in the realms of time⟦/Q⟧" [21:5.10]. Here lies the ground on which we can commune with Jesus through the Spirit of Truth.

6. Future Destiny: The Way, the Truth, and the Life

The revelators believe that each Michael is the absolute of the dual-deity concepts of his origin and embodies actual phases of the infinity of the Father and the Son [21:6.1]. The completion of the bestowal career signifies the appearance of a capacity for service transcending the finite, and they see the restriction on creating new creatures as made necessary by the liberation of these superfinite potentials [21:6.2]. In the far future, in the universes of outer space, the union of a Master Son and a seventh-stage Creative Spirit may attain to service on subabsolute levels [21:6.3]. And the revelators believe that in eternity the Michaels are literally destined to be "⟦Q 21:6.4⟧the way, the truth, and the life⟦/Q⟧," lighting the path for all universe personalities [21:6.4].

Summary

Master Michael rules his universe with a supreme sovereignty that synthesizes the viewpoint of Deity and the experience of the creature [21:5.1-5]; instead of new creation he fosters the life that already exists and communicates with all his worlds through the Spirit of Truth [21:5.6, 21:5.10]. Under his rule, justice prevails after mercy has been exhausted [21:5.7]. His future is service beyond the finite, to be forever the way, the truth, and the life of all personalities [21:6.2-4].

q180.question: What does the story of the Celestial Guardians and High Son Assistants, trinitized without experience, envying ascending mortals teach us?
q180.answer:
The Celestial Guardians and High Son Assistants are creature-trinitized sons: offspring trinitized by perfected humans and by Paradise-Havona personalities, who were then embraced by the Paradise Trinity [22:9.1]. Because they have not personally passed through the ascending career, they are marvelous beings and yet deficient in experience [22:9.6]. The Mighty Messenger who tells this story says that, seeing them look so longingly even at those newly arrived on the mansion worlds, he could not help realizing that they really envied their supposedly less fortunate brethren who walk the path of experience [22:9.8].

This passage shows how precious "actual experience" is in the universe, and teaches us to be grateful for our lowly origin.

1. Who They Are and How They Are Assigned

The creature-trinitized sons are embraced by the Trinity in groups of seven thousand, and they are assigned to the superuniverses on the recommendation of their former teachers, the Trinity Teacher Sons [22:9.1]. Those who have shown more satisfactory service become High Son Assistants, and those less distinguished become Celestial Guardians [22:9.1]. They are versed in the affairs of the ascending career, not by having ascended themselves, but as a result of serving with the Trinity Teacher Sons [22:9.2].

2. The Celestial Guardians: Officers of the Superuniverse Courts

There are almost one billion Celestial Guardians in Orvonton, assigned chiefly to the major sector headquarters [22:9.3]. As officers of the courts of the Ancients of Days they function as court messengers and bearers of summons and decisions, and they are the apprehending agents who bring in the beings required to appear before the superuniverse judges [22:9.4]. They have never been indwelt by Adjusters, nor are they Spirit fused or Son fused, but the embrace of the Trinity compensates for their nonfused status [22:9.5].

3. The High Son Assistants: Ideas Personified

The High Son Assistants are the personality embodiment of some divine idea, some universal ideal, as it has never before been conceived or trinitized [22:10.2]. The book says, "⟦Q 22:10.2⟧They are that idea personified⟦/Q⟧" [22:10.2]. Therefore, in dealing with problems concerning that idea, they are inexpressibly useful, and the revelator recalls how keenly he realized their value in the work of commissions [22:10.4]. They are touchingly affectionate and loyal, supremely wise concerning their one idea, yet humble beings who seek knowledge in other fields even from ascending mortals [22:10.8].

4. Nothing Takes the Place of Experience

Their limitation lies in the fact that their experiential capacity is time-space inhibited [22:9.7]. The book declares: "⟦Q 22:9.7⟧There is simply nothing in all universal existence which can take the place of actual personal experience⟦/Q⟧" [22:9.7]. They are held in reserve for experiential function in a future universe age [22:9.7]. Thus they are neither as versatile nor as dependable as the ascenders, and they lack the profound personal experience of those who have climbed up to glory from the dark domains of space [22:9.6].

5. Gratitude for Our Origin

The revelator, who has an ascending career, confesses that they love these beings and try to compensate their deficiencies, "⟦Q 22:9.6⟧but they make us ever grateful for our lowly origin and our capacity for experience⟦/Q⟧" [22:9.6]. Their willingness to acknowledge their deficiencies is said to be transcendently beautiful and sometimes most touchingly pathetic [22:9.6]. The trials and struggles we pass through now are precious assets that other beings envy.

6. We Too Can Take Part in Trinitization

Because the High Son Assistants are so valuable in superuniverse administration, Uversa encourages the pilgrims of space and the Paradise residents to attempt trinitization after they have contributed to each other the needed experience [22:10.6]. The experience of today may become the groundwork from which a new being is brought forth in the distant future.

Summary

The Celestial Guardians and High Son Assistants are creature-trinitized sons embraced by the Trinity who serve preciously in the superuniverse government but lack the actual experience of ascension [22:9.1-6, 22:10.1-2]. Therefore they envy the mortals who walk the path of experience [22:9.8], and from them we learn the truth that nothing takes the place of experience, and the reason to be grateful for our lowly origin [22:9.6-7].

q181.question: What are the Census Directors, and how do they record a person's birth and death?
q181.answer:
The Census Directors are a special and completed creation of the Infinite Spirit, charged with keeping count of all will creatures in the universe [24:2.2]. Although the cosmic mind already knows of the existence and whereabouts of every thinking creature, there operates in the universe of universes a separate, independent technique for counting all will creatures [24:2.1]. They were created to be in perfect synchrony with the reflectivity technique of the superuniverses, and at the same time they are personally sensitive and responsive to intelligent will [24:2.2].

The key point is that what the Census Directors record is not "the birth and death of the body" but "the appearance and the last exercise of will."

1. They Know the Instant Will Appears

By a technique not wholly understood, the Census Directors are aware of the birth of will anywhere in the grand universe the instant it occurs [24:2.2]. They are therefore always competent to report at once the number, nature, and whereabouts of the will creatures in any part of the central creation and the seven superuniverses [24:2.2]. They do not, however, function on Paradise, for there knowledge is inherent and the Deities know all [24:2.2].

2. The First and the Last Act of Will

"⟦Q 24:2.8⟧Census Directors register the existence of a new will creature when the first act of will is performed; they indicate the death of a will creature when the last act of will takes place⟦/Q⟧" [24:2.8]. The partial emergence of will seen in certain of the higher animals does not belong to their domain; they keep count of nothing but bona fide will creatures [24:2.8]. Exactly how they register the function of will, even the revelator does not know [24:2.8]. This illustrates well the view of The Urantia Book that the essence of being human lies in will, the capacity to choose.

3. Organization: From Havona to the Local Universes

Seven Census Directors are stationed one on the pilot world of each Havona circuit, and all the other directors operate under the jurisdiction of the Ancients of Days [24:2.3]. One director presides at each superuniverse headquarters, and under him numerous directors are stationed at the capital of each local universe [24:2.4]. In Orvonton, the seventh superuniverse, there are one hundred thousand Census Directors available for assignment to the local universes [24:2.5]. Usatia, the chief of Orvonton, does not register intelligent will directly but functions as the tabulating personality who compiles the reports coming in from each local creation [24:2.5]. These census data belong to the superuniverse and are not transmitted to Havona or Paradise [24:2.6].

4. Counters, Not Recorders

The Census Directors are concerned with human beings only to the extent of recording the fact of will function [24:2.7]. They are not concerned with the records of a person's life and doings, and they are not in any sense recording personalities [24:2.7]. There is therefore no need to mistake them for beings who keep watch over our conduct.

5. One Who Knows Me at This Very Moment

The book tells us a remarkable fact. The Census Director of Nebadon, now stationed on Salvington, "⟦Q 24:2.7⟧is at this very moment personally conscious and aware of your living presence here on Urantia⟦/Q⟧" [24:2.7], and the moment we cease to function as will creatures he will at once afford the records confirmation of our death [24:2.7]. It is a comfort that in so vast a universe one person's existence is known in such a personal way.

6. Infallible Individuals

These beings have always been Census Directors and always will be; they are relatively useless for other work, but in their own function they are infallible [24:2.9]. They are never negligent and they never falsify, and despite their marvelous powers they are individuals with recognizable spirit presence and form [24:2.9].

Summary

The Census Directors are beings created by the Infinite Spirit who, synchronized with reflectivity, know the number, nature, and whereabouts of all will creatures in the universe [24:2.2]. They register a person's existence at the first act of will and record his death at the last act of will [24:2.8], but they do not record his doings [24:2.7]. Even now the Census Director of Nebadon knows the living presence of each one of us [24:2.7].

q182.question: Who are the Graduate Guides who lead ascenders in Havona, and how did they come into being?
q182.answer:
The Graduate Guides are among the higher personalities of the Infinite Spirit, devoted to the task of piloting the mortal graduates from the superuniverses of time through the Havona course of education and training [24:6.1]. They conduct the high university of technical instruction and spiritual training that mortals need in order to reach the goal of the ages, God, rest, and the eternity of perfected service, and they prepare the ascending pilgrims to enter Paradise and the Corps of the Finality [24:6.1].

Their origin is something of a mystery, but the revelators believe that they are transformed beings who were formerly experienced members of the Havona Servitals [24:6.4, 24:7.1].

1. A Guide Who Accompanies You throughout Havona

The guide who greets us upon our arrival on the receiving world of the outer Havona circuit will be with us throughout our career on the heavenly circuits [24:6.3]. He follows us to the end of the Havona course and witnesses our falling into the last sleep of time, the transit to Paradise [24:6.3]. When we awaken from that sleep, a Paradise Companion greets us [24:6.3]. The Graduate Guides never leave the Havona worlds, and unless we reject the plan, we shall someday meet these noble beings face to face [24:6.9].

2. The First Guide, Malvorian, and the First Pilgrim, Grandfanda

There was no record of a Graduate Guide until the day when the first mortal pilgrim reached the outer belt of the central creation [24:6.4]. The instant that first pilgrim arrived on the pilot world of the outer circuit, he met Malvorian, the first of the Graduate Guides, who is now the chief of their supreme council [24:6.4]. The name of this pilgrim discoverer of Havona is Grandfanda, and his arrival was the signal for the establishment of the broadcast service of the universe of universes [24:6.8]. When the first pilgrim arrived, "⟦Q 24:6.7⟧the thrill of all time swept through the heavenly courts⟦/Q⟧" [24:6.7].

3. From Havona Servitals to Graduate Guides

Evolution is not the order of the central universe, yet the revelators believe that the Graduate Guides are the perfected or experienced members of the Havona Servitals [24:7.1]. This is because their broad sympathy and their ability to understand ascending creatures appear to have been gained by actual service in the superuniverses [24:7.1]. It happens that an experienced servital, returning from a superuniverse assignment, has personal contact with the central Paradise radiance, is embraced, and is never seen again [24:7.2]. Then, within exactly three moments, a little less than three days of our time, a newly born Graduate Guide appears on the outer circuit of Havona, and their number is exactly equal to the number of servitals who have disappeared [24:7.6]. The special attachment the two orders have for each other also supports this inference [24:7.7].

4. The Participation of the Supreme Being

The Havona Servitals are created by the Seven Master Spirits in co-operation with the Supreme Power Directors, and so they inherently relate to phases of Supremacy [24:7.8]. The revelators believe that this transformation occurs in response to the will of the Infinite Spirit acting for the Supreme, and they surmise that, although the Supreme Being does not create the Graduate Guides, he participates in some way [24:7.8]. With the arrival of the mortal ascenders, extensive modifications began in the organization of the central universe, and the appearance of the Graduate Guides is an act of God the Supreme signifying those modifications [24:7.9].

5. What It Means for Us

The revelator says that the activities of the Graduate Guides are so superspiritual that they are difficult to portray to the material mind, but that we shall understand them when our vision is enlarged on the mansion worlds, and that the range of our spiritual understanding is not destined always to be so limited [24:6.2]. The fact that even the perfect central universe brought forth new beings in order to receive the children of time shows how great a meaning our ascension has for the whole universe.

Summary

The Graduate Guides are beings who instruct and accompany ascending mortals throughout the seven circuits of Havona [24:6.1, 24:6.3]. They first appeared, with Malvorian, when the first pilgrim, Grandfanda, arrived [24:6.4, 24:6.8], and they are regarded as experienced Havona Servitals transformed through the divine embrace [24:7.1-6]. Their appearance was the Supreme Being's response for the reception of evolutionary creatures [24:7.9].

q183.question: What kind of beings are the "Universal Conciliators," said to settle disputes between worlds, and how do they work?
q183.answer:
The Universal Conciliators are beings created in each superuniverse: each time a Havona Servital is created, one Conciliator comes into being in each superuniverse, seven in all [25:2.1]. When a Master Spirit, in union with the Power Directors, creates a Havona Servital, there is a focalization in one of the Reflective Spirits of each superuniverse, and an equal number of Conciliators appear in full-fledged form at the headquarters of that superuniverse [25:2.2]. They serve as traveling courts that promptly adjudicate the minor difficulties of the universe of universes so that it may run in an orderly manner [25:2.11].

1. A Conciliating Commission of Four in One

The Conciliators are inherently divided into groups of four, three of them spiritual personalities and one a semimaterial being [25:2.5]. The group consists of a judge-arbiter, a spirit-advocate, a divine executioner, and a recorder [25:2.6-9]. The judge-arbiter is designated by the unanimous vote of the other three; the spirit-advocate protects the rights of all persons concerned and presents the evidence; the divine executioner makes contact with material beings and carries out the decisions; and the recorder makes all the records [25:2.6-9]. While court is in session, the spirit-advocate drops out and three function, and so they are also called "referee trios" [25:2.10].

2. They Do Not Deal with Eternal Issues

The Conciliators traverse space at three times the speed of seraphim, and without such commissions the tribunals of the worlds would be hopelessly congested with minor misunderstandings [25:2.11]. But "⟦Q 25:2.12⟧These referee trios do not pass upon matters of eternal import⟦/Q⟧" [25:2.12]. The soul and eternal prospects of a creature of time are never placed in jeopardy by their decisions [25:2.12]. Once a commission has accepted jurisdiction, its rulings are final and unanimous, and there is no appeal [25:2.12].

3. Seven Stages of Service, from the Worlds to the Superuniverse

The Conciliators begin as conciliators to the worlds and are promoted to serve as conciliators to the system headquarters, the constellations, the local universes, the superuniverse minor sectors, the major sectors, and the superuniverse [25:3.3-13]. The young and less experienced commissions begin their service on lowly worlds such as Urantia [25:3.1]. On a world, when one person from each of the contending parties files a petition, the commission functions at once [25:3.3], and it makes no decision until all the evidence has been heard [25:3.4]. The divine executioners are "⟦Q 25:3.5⟧masterful manipulators of that which is in the interests of that which ought to be⟦/Q⟧" [25:3.5], and they sometimes act in strange ways without defying natural law.

4. From Judges to Teachers

As they go to higher levels, their task changes. There is less and less misunderstanding to arbitrate and more and more mysterious phenomena to interpret and explain, so that they evolve from arbiters of differences to explainers of mysteries, from judges to interpretative teachers [25:3.12]. The book says: "⟦Q 25:3.12⟧The higher a creature's education, the more respect he has for the knowledge, experience, and opinions of others⟦/Q⟧" [25:3.12]. At the superuniverse stage, the divine executioner loses his punitive powers and becomes the physical voice of the spirit trio [25:3.13].

5. Why Conciliation Is Needed in the Universe

The moment the Creators create evolutionary beings with the power of choice, misunderstandings are certain to arise, and provision is needed for the fair adjustment of honest differences of opinion [25:3.7]. The Creators could have made the local universes as perfect as Havona, but they did not; they made universes rich in differences and difficulties, and at the same time provided the means for harmonizing them [25:3.7]. The conflicts in our own lives are likewise part of a universe design for growth, and to seek fair conciliation is to follow the way of the universe.

6. Four Who Are Together Forever

The members of a conciliating commission are never separated; they serve together forever just as they were originally associated [25:3.17]. "⟦Q 25:3.17⟧They are eternally associated as the embodiment of the supreme justice of time and space⟦/Q⟧" [25:3.17]. Not one Conciliator has ever gone astray; they are not infallible in judgment, but they are infallible in faithfulness [25:3.2].

Summary

The Universal Conciliators are beings who come into existence in each superuniverse along with the creation of the Havona Servitals, and four of them, a judge-arbiter, a spirit-advocate, a divine executioner, and a recorder, form one commission [25:2.1-9]. They adjudicate the disputes of time, not of eternal destiny, promptly and fairly [25:2.11-12], and as they rise from the worlds to the superuniverse they grow from judges into teachers [25:3.3-13]. Their existence shows the wisdom of the Creators, who would harmonize the differences that free will brings forth [25:3.7].

q184.question: What kind of beings are the Morontia Companions and the Paradise Companions who receive us on the ascending journey, and what do they do?
q184.answer:
The Urantia Book says that the ascending journey does not consist only of study and testing, but that a ministry of friendship and companionship is provided all along the way. The chief examples are the Morontia Companions of the local universe and the Paradise Companions of Paradise. The Morontia Companions are offspring of the local universe Mother Spirits and are the friends and associates of all who live the morontia life [25:7.1], while the Paradise Companions are beings chosen from the angelic hosts to become personality associates of ascenders on Paradise [25:8.1, 25:8.3].

Neither kind of companion is charged with work essential to ascension, yet for that very reason they reveal the thoughtful love of God.

1. The Morontia Companions: Friends in the Local Universe

The Morontia Companions are not indispensable to the actual progress of the ascenders, nor do they take the place of the seraphic guardians who accompany mortals on the Paradise journey [25:7.1]. They provide gracious hospitality to those who are just beginning the long ascent, and they are excellent sponsors of play, assisted by the reversion directors [25:7.1]. Since they serve only in the local universe, when we finish the morontia career and depart for the superuniverse we will truly regret that they cannot accompany us [25:7.3].

2. Rest and Play Are Also Part of the Ascent

The book says that on the morontia training worlds we must carry on serious and increasingly difficult tasks, but that there will always be opportunities for regular rest and reversion [25:7.2]. Throughout the whole journey toward Paradise there are times of rest and spirit play, and even in the career of light and life there is always time for worship and for new achievements [25:7.2]. The spiritual life includes not only tension and effort but also rest and joy.

3. The Paradise Companions: Beings Who Exist Only to Be With Us

The Paradise Companions are chosen from among the seraphim, seconaphim, supernaphim, and omniaphim [25:8.1]; they are nominated by the local universe Mother Spirits, the superuniverse Reflective Spirits, and Majeston of Paradise, and commissioned by one of the Seven Master Spirits [25:8.2]. Except for permanent status, this service is the highest honor conferred on ministering spirits [25:8.2]. They have nothing especial to accomplish on behalf of those with whom they fraternize; "⟦Q 25:8.3⟧they are simply companions⟦/Q⟧" [25:8.3]. Almost every other being on Paradise will have something to do for us, but these are assigned only to be with us and to commune with us as personality associates [25:8.3].

4. "Not Good for Man to Be Alone"

Mortals come from races that are very social, and because the Creators well know that it is "⟦Q 25:8.4⟧not good for man to be alone⟦/Q⟧," provision is made for companionship even on Paradise [25:8.4]. If we arrive together with a close associate from earth or with our guardian seraphim, no permanent companion is assigned, but if we arrive alone, a companion welcomes us when we awaken from the last sleep of time [25:8.5]. The receiving companions have reviewed our ascension records beforehand and are well versed in the careers of the arriving pilgrims [25:8.6]. Moreover, an ascender is never assigned a companion of a nature different from his own superuniverse type [25:8.8].

5. Companionship for Those Who Fail

When an ascender fails in the Deity adventure in Havona and must return to the universes of time, one of the Paradise Companions is assigned to go with him, to comfort and encourage him, until he returns to resume the ascent [25:8.9]. If the pilgrim had been accompanied by his guardian seraphim, that seraphim is permitted to volunteer to go back with him [25:8.10]. When only one of two closely associated ascenders succeeds, the successful one is not permitted to go back even if he wishes to; instead a companion accompanies the one who failed, and the successful one teaches on Paradise while awaiting the return of his associate [25:8.11].

Summary

The Morontia Companions provide hospitality, play, and friendship to ascenders in the local universe [25:7.1-3], and the Paradise Companions are angels assigned on Paradise only to be with us [25:8.1-3]. This provision springs from the Creators' understanding that it is not good for man to be alone [25:8.4], and a companion goes even with the pilgrim who fails [25:8.9]. God's plan cares not only for our achievement but even for our loneliness.

q185.question: If an ascending pilgrim fails in the Deity adventure in Havona, what happens, and why is that failure not regarded as defeat?
q185.answer:
The ascending pilgrims passing through the seven circuits of Havona set out, circuit by circuit, on the "Deity adventure" of recognizing and attaining, in turn, the Infinite Spirit, the Eternal Son, and the Universal Father. The Urantia Book reveals that nearly all succeed in this adventure, but that occasionally a pilgrim fails to attain on the first attempt [26:8.4]. Yet this failure is by no means the end. The pilgrim who fails returns for a time to the universes of time to serve, then comes back to the same circuit and tries again, and on the second attempt he always succeeds [26:8.5].

The book sums up the attitude of heaven toward such an event in these words: "⟦Q 26:8.3⟧On Paradise, disappointment is never regarded as defeat; postponement is never looked upon as disgrace⟦/Q⟧" [26:8.3], and the apparent failures of time are never confused with the significant delays of eternity.

1. Who Fails, and Where

After the attainment of the Infinite Spirit there are no more examinations; the tests of the inner circles are the very performances of the pilgrims while in the embrace of the Deities, and advancement is determined purely by the spirituality of the individual [26:8.3]. Nearly all attain the Infinite Spirit, though pilgrims from the first superuniverse occasionally fail on the first attempt; those who actually fail in the search for the Son come almost entirely from the third and fifth superuniverses, and most of those who fail to attain the Father come from the sixth superuniverse [26:8.4]. The book regards this as pointing to good and sufficient reasons for these unavoidable delays [26:8.4]. The cause of failure lies not in the spirit itself but in some phase of the technique of approach or of the experiential background; the spirit of such candidates was wholly acceptable [26:10.3].

2. Right after Failure: Comfort on the Second Circle

Those who are unsuccessful in the first effort at Deity attainment are advanced directly to the second circle before being returned to superuniverse service, and there the counselors and advisers become the counselors and comforters of these disappointed pilgrims [26:10.2]. The book says that this disappointment differs in no way, except in its magnitude, from the long list of experiences on which they had climbed, as on a ladder, from chaos to glory [26:10.2]. After a long sojourn on the second circle they are examined by the councils of perfection and certified as having passed the Havona tests, and as regards their nonspirit status they receive the same standing as those who actually succeeded [26:10.3]. When a pilgrim who came to Havona alone fails, a Paradise Companion is assigned to accompany him, comforting and encouraging him until his return [25:8.9].

3. The Return to Service and the Second Adventure

The failing candidates are returned to the work of the realms of space for not less than one millennium, under the jurisdiction of the conductors of assignment of the primary supernaphim, going not to their native superuniverse but to the supercreation best suited for their retraining [26:8.5]. Led by their counselors, they stand before the conductors of assignment and return to the service of time, but they go in joy and gladness [26:10.4]. The author of the book testifies that he has observed them serving as the highest type of loving ministrators to those who experience temporary disappointments [26:10.2]. When their service is finished they return of their own accord to the outer circuit of Havona and prepare again from the circle where their career was interrupted; on the second attempt the same supernaphim ministers are with them, and these never fail to pilot their charges to success [26:8.5, 26:10.4].

4. Lessons for Our Spiritual Life

The book says that the pilgrim who reaches Havona already possesses a faith that disappointment cannot shake, so that even failure to discern the Universal Father cannot disturb that trust [26:4.13]. Long before coming to Havona they had learned "⟦Q 26:5.3⟧to feast upon uncertainty, to fatten upon disappointment⟦/Q⟧" [26:5.3] and to enthuse over apparent defeat. Their battle cry was that in liaison with God nothing is impossible [26:5.3]. The fact that in the event of failure no reasons are ever assigned, and that neither the candidates nor their tutors are ever chided or criticized [26:8.3], shows that heaven's way of dealing with failure is not judgment but patience and retraining.

Summary

The pilgrim who fails in the Deity adventure of Havona is comforted on the second circle and certified as having passed the tests, then serves joyfully in the worlds of space for not less than a millennium, and returns to succeed without fail on the second attempt [26:8.5, 26:10.2-10.4]. That failure is not a defect of spirit but only a "delay" arising from questions of technique and experience [26:10.3], and Paradise never regards disappointment as defeat or postponement as disgrace [26:8.3]. This teaching reminds us that the disappointments we meet now may also be one rung on the ladder of ascension.

q186.question: What is the meaning of the "last rest" that the ascending pilgrim enters on the final circuit of Havona, and what are the roles of the complements of rest and the instigators of rest?
q186.answer:
The mortal ascender falls into the last sleep of time on the innermost circuit of Havona and awakens to life everlasting on the shores of Paradise. The Urantia Book describes this sleep not as mere slumber but as a rest of metamorphosis that changes a "creature of time" into a "denizen of eternity" [27:1.3]. The beings who assist this decisive transition are the complements of rest, the last order of secondary supernaphim, and the instigators of rest, the first order of primary supernaphim [26:10.7, 27:1.1].

The book states the meaning of this transition thus: "⟦Q 26:11.8⟧Your first transition was indeed death, the second an ideal sleep, and now the third metamorphosis is the true rest⟦/Q⟧" [26:11.8], that is, the relaxation of the ages.

1. The Sevenfold Nature of Rest

The book explains that rest is of a sevenfold nature [27:1.2]. In the lower orders of life there is the rest of sleep and of play; in higher beings, the rest of discovery; and in the highest type of spirit personality, the rest of worship. There is also the rest of energy intake, the recharging with physical or spiritual energy, and the transit sleep when enseraphimed in passage from one sphere to another [27:1.2]. Entirely different from all of these is the deep sleep of metamorphosis, the transition rest from one state of existence to another, which always attends a change of actual universe status [27:1.2].

2. The Complements of Rest: Companions Who Keep You from Sleeping Alone

Much of the ascender's time on the last circuit is spent studying the problems of the impending Paradise residence, and the complements of rest help with adjustment to Paradise through association with the diverse groups of beings there [26:11.1, 26:11.3]. They are concerned less with the training of the pilgrims than with fostering understanding association among the various groups [26:11.3]. And when the time comes to sleep, you do not go alone to your rest as in the sleep of mortal death or in the transit trance to Havona [26:11.7]. Your long-time associate of the first circle, the complement of rest, moves over by your side and enters the rest as one with you; this is the pledge of Havona that your transition is complete and that only the final touches of perfection remain [26:11.7].

3. The Instigators of Rest: Those Who Induce the Sleep and Greet the Awakening

The instigators of rest are the inspectors of Paradise who go forth from the central Isle to the inner circuit of Havona to collaborate with the complements of rest [27:1.1]. The book says, "⟦Q 27:1.1⟧The one essential to the enjoyment of Paradise is rest, divine rest⟦/Q⟧" [27:1.1], and introduces them as the final instructors who make ready the pilgrims of time for eternity. They first meet the pilgrims toward the end of their sojourn on the first circle and complete the preparation for the transition sleep of the final resurrection [26:11.6]. On awakening in repersonalization on Paradise, the ascender at once recognizes that the instigator of rest who greets him on the shore is the very supernaphim who induced the last sleep [27:1.4].

4. The Door to Becoming a Child of Eternity

The book says that no one is truly a Paradise child until he has crossed the inner circuit and experienced the resurrection of eternity from the last sleep of time [26:11.6]. Only those who thus fall asleep on the first circle of Havona and awaken on the shores of Paradise are children of eternity; others go as guests without residential status [26:11.6]. Just as seraphim are indispensable to mortal survival, the instigators of rest and the complements of rest are indispensable to this transcending metamorphosis [27:1.3]. The awakened ascender remembers the last supreme stretch of faith with which he once more committed the keeping of his identity into the hands of the Universal Father [27:1.4].

Summary

The last rest on the inner circuit of Havona is the third transition, following death and the transit sleep; it is the sleep of metamorphosis that changes a creature of time and space into an eternal resident of Paradise [26:11.8, 27:1.3]. The complement of rest, as a long-time companion, sleeps alongside and pledges the completion of the transition, while the instigator of rest induces that sleep and greets the awakened one on the shores of eternity [26:11.7, 27:1.4]. The ascender entrusts himself to the Father in this sleep as a final act of faith, and then awakens to the life everlasting of which it is said: "⟦Q 27:1.5⟧And there shall be no more sleep⟦/Q⟧." [27:1.5]

q187.question: In the account of the conductors of worship on Paradise, what does The Urantia Book teach that worship is, and what does it mean for us now?
q187.answer:
Paper 27 of The Urantia Book, in introducing the conductors of worship, the seventh order of primary supernaphim, gives its clearest definition of the essence of worship. The book says, "⟦Q 27:7.1⟧Worship is the highest privilege and the first duty of all created intelligences⟦/Q⟧." [27:7.1], and explains that worship is the conscious and joyous act of recognizing and acknowledging the truth and fact of the intimate and personal relationships of the Creators with their creatures [27:7.1].

Worship, then, is at once a duty and a joy, an experience that grows larger and wider the more deeply one knows God. It would not be too much to say that the whole ascension career moves toward the fullness of this worship.

1. The Quality of Worship Depends on the Depth of Perception

The quality of worship is determined by the depth of creature perception, and as the knowledge of the infinite character of the Gods grows, the act of worship becomes increasingly all-encompassing [27:7.1]. In the end it attains the highest experiential delight and the most exquisite pleasure known to created beings [27:7.1]. As the circuits of Havona are passed one by one, worship becomes an ever-growing passion, until on Paradise it becomes necessary to direct and otherwise control its expression [27:7.2].

2. All of Paradise a Single Sanctuary

There are several places of worship on the Isle of Paradise, but the Isle itself is more like one vast sanctuary of divine service [27:7.2]. Worship is the first and dominant passion of all who climb up to its shores, the spontaneous effervescence of beings who have learned enough about God to attain his presence [27:7.2]. Even with set times and places of worship, these cannot accommodate the overflowing emotions of beings who have struggled up from the spiritual darkness of the lower worlds, and the book says that personalities perfect by nature can never fully appreciate their response [27:7.6].

3. What the Conductors of Worship Do

The outpourings of adoration and praise on Paradise take place under the direction of the conductors of worship [27:7.3]. Every ascending being would delight to remain forever in the attitude of worship, so the directors of assignment must periodically disperse the assemblies, and no ascending being is required to enter upon the assignments of eternal service until he has attained full satisfaction in worship [27:7.3]. The conductors of worship teach how to worship so as to gain the satisfaction of self-expression while still giving attention to the essential activities of Paradise; otherwise it would take the average mortal hundreds of years to express his full gratitude [27:7.4]. All the arts of the whole universe that can intensify self-expression and the conveyance of appreciation are employed in this worship [27:7.5].

4. The Fruit of Worship and the Corps of the Finality

When the hearts of the Gods are fully satisfied by the sincere worship of the residents, the light of the Deity abode flashes in threefold pulsations, and the book calls it the great fruit of the plan of the Gods that the intelligent love of the creature satisfies the infinite love of the Creator Father [27:7.7]. Only after attaining the supreme satisfaction of the fullness of worship is the ascender qualified for admission to the Corps of the Finality, and the seventh jubilee celebrates this [27:7.8]. The conductors of worship are the last supernaphim to bid farewell to the ascender when he takes the Trinity oath and is mustered into the Corps of Mortal Finaliters [27:7.9].

5. Worship Here and Now

The book says that the mode of worship on Paradise is beyond mortal comprehension, but that its spirit can begin to be appreciated even here on Urantia, because the spirits of the Gods even now indwell us, hover over us, and inspire us to true worship [27:7.5]. It also says, "⟦Q 27:7.5⟧What play does for your jaded minds on earth, worship will do for your perfected souls on Paradise⟦/Q⟧." [27:7.5], showing that worship is a joy that brings new strength.

Summary

Worship as The Urantia Book describes it is the joyous acknowledgment of our personal relationship with God, the highest privilege and the first duty of all intelligences [27:7.1]. Worship deepens the more we know God, becomes the highest joy on Paradise, and only on attaining full satisfaction in worship does eternal service as a finaliter begin [27:7.3, 27:7.8]. Its spirit begins to grow even now on this earth through the spirit that indwells us [27:7.5].

q188.question: Unlike the ascenders who come and go in the local universe, who are the "permanent citizens" who always remain there, and why are they needed?
q188.answer:
The mortal ascender is a pilgrim who keeps moving onward, from the mansion worlds through Salvington to the superuniverse, and on to Havona and Paradise. But Paper 37 of The Urantia Book says that the local universe, like the superuniverse and the central universe, has its orders of "permanent citizenship" [37:9.1]. They are the Susatia, the Univitatia, the Material Sons, and the midway creatures, who, together with the Spirit-fused ascenders and the Spironga, make up a relatively permanent citizenry [37:9.2-9.6].

These beings, as a rule, neither ascend nor descend, but continually contribute to the universe the experience they have accumulated on the level of their origin [37:9.6]. Their part is to give continuity and experiential wisdom to a universe administration whose personnel is constantly changing.

1. The Permanent Residents of Each Administrative Unit

The book summarizes that every division of the administrative organization has its residents of citizenship status [37:9.12]. Urantia has its midwayers; Jerusem, the system capital, has its Material Sons and Daughters; Edentia, the constellation headquarters, has its Univitatia; and the citizens of Salvington are of two kinds, the created Susatia and the evolved Spirit-fused mortals [37:9.12]. Uversa, the superuniverse headquarters, has its Abandonters; Havona has its native beings; and Paradise has its Paradise Citizens [37:9.12].

2. The Susatia and the Univitatia

The Susatia are the glorious offspring of the Creator Son and the Creative Spirit; they reside on Salvington as permanent citizens and are closely associated with the Spirit-fused mortals of the Nebadon corps of perfection [37:9.7]. The Univitatia are nonreproducing beings who minister on the one hundred constellation headquarters spheres, existing on a plane of life about midway between the semimaterial status of the Material Sons and the spirit level of the Susatia [37:9.8]. The book says that the Univitatia do for the ascending mortals passing through the constellation spheres what the Havona natives do for the pilgrims of the central universe [37:9.8].

3. The Material Sons and the Midway Creatures

The Material Sons and Daughters are the reproducing order of sonship created by the Creator Son as he personalizes his final concept of being in dual form; their offspring live as permanent citizens of the system capitals, and some are commissioned as Planetary Adams [37:9.9]. The midway creatures are the only group of intelligent beings who remain continuously on a planet from the days of the Planetary Prince to the far-distant time of its settling in light and life [37:9.11]. We mortals are short-lived residents who are born, live, die, and pass on to other worlds, and the assignments of celestial ministers are also transient; but the book says, "⟦Q 37:9.11⟧On Urantia the midway ministers are in reality the actual custodians of the planet⟦/Q⟧" [37:9.11], and explains that they provide continuity of planetary administration.

4. The Spirit-fused Mortals: Evolved Permanent Citizens

The Spirit-fused mortals, the other citizens of Salvington, do not attain Paradise, but in dealing with the problems of Nebadon they achieve an experiential wisdom surpassing anything attained by the ascenders who are passing through [37:5.11]. Those of them who become High Commissioners begin as racial commissioners on the planets, representing the viewpoints and needs of the human races, and act as advisers in all tribunals [37:5.5, 37:5.7]. The book says that "⟦Q 37:5.9⟧they are always present to speak for those who cannot be present to speak for themselves⟦/Q⟧" [37:5.9].

5. Why Permanent Citizens Are Needed

The book explains that the plan limiting the ascent of Spirit-fused mortals benefits the local universe by insuring it a permanent evolutionary population that will continue to stabilize and diversify local universe administration with ever-increasing experience [37:5.11]. If all mortals departed for Paradise, the local universe and superuniverse tribunals would depend solely on the service of those who are passing through, so it is entirely fitting that there be a permanent ascending citizenry [40:10.4]. The authoritative wisdom that ripens in the faithful service of such local universe citizens is a decisive factor in the settling of a local universe [40:10.6].

Summary

The permanent citizens of the local universe are the Susatia and the Spirit-fused mortals of Salvington, the Univitatia of Edentia, the Material Sons and Daughters of Jerusem, and the midway creatures of the planets [37:9.2-9.5, 37:9.12]. While the ascenders keep passing through, these remain in their places and provide continuity of administration and experiential wisdom [37:9.6, 37:9.11], and thanks to them the local universe can at last be settled in light and life [37:5.11, 40:10.6].

q189.question: Please explain in order the "seven stages of the ascending mortal" set out in Paper 30 of The Urantia Book, from the planet to Paradise.
q189.answer:
Section 4 of Paper 30 summarizes in seven stages the universe career of an Adjuster-indwelt mortal from birth on a planet to arrival on Paradise. The seven stages are: planetary mortals, sleeping survivors, mansion world students, morontia progressors, superuniverse wards, Havona pilgrims, and Paradise arrivals [30:4.2-4.8]. The book tells this story with reference to Adjuster-fused mortals, explaining that all the races of Urantia may look forward to such a destiny [30:4.9].

In terms of bodily form, these seven stages are a journey of transformation from a creature of flesh and blood to a morontia being, and then from an evolving spirit to a perfected spirit [30:4.26].

1. Planetary Mortals and Sleeping Survivors

All mortals are evolutionary beings of animal origin with ascendant potential, and the human races of every world enjoy the same ministry of the Sons of God and the presence of the ministering spirits [30:4.10]. Among mortals of survival status, those who have attained the level that merits personal guardians are personalized on the mansion worlds in the third period, but the others rest in unconscious sleep until the coming of a Son of God at the end of the dispensation [30:4.11]. To these sleepers the passing of time is of no consequence; one who has slept five thousand years reacts no differently from one who has rested five days [30:4.12].

2. Mansion World Students and the Resurrection

All survivors who reawaken on the mansion worlds are mansion world students [30:4.14]. The physical body returns to the earth; the Adjuster keeps the spirit transcript of the mind, and the seraphim keep the immortal soul, and the resurrection takes place when the two reassemble what they hold in trust [30:4.15]. Each local system, made up of about one thousand inhabited planets, has seven mansion worlds [30:4.16], and it was to such training worlds that Jesus referred when he said, "⟦Q 30:4.17⟧In my Father's house are many mansions⟦/Q⟧." [30:4.17]

3. Morontia Progressors

While ascending from the mansion worlds through the spheres of the system, the constellation, and the local universe, mortals are called morontia progressors, and they serve in various assignments together with their teachers and older brethren [30:4.18]. Throughout this period they are wards of the local universe [30:4.19]. Just before leaving the local universe headquarters they attain true spirit identity; this is only a minor transition, for mind, personality, and character are unchanged, and only the form is altered [30:4.20]. At this time they receive spirit confirmation from the Creator Son and the Mother Spirit, and no superuniverse ward has ever been known to go astray [30:4.21].

4. Superuniverse Wards and Havona Pilgrims

On arriving at the training worlds of the superuniverse, the ascender becomes a ward of the Ancients of Days, climbs through the cultural spheres of the minor sectors, the major sectors, and the superuniverse headquarters, and thoroughly learns local universe and superuniverse administration [30:4.22-4.24]. When spirit development is complete, he prepares for the long flight to Havona; this journey is always made alone, and from here on instruction is personal and individual [30:4.26, 30:4.27]. The first act of the Havona career is to thank the transport seconaphim, and then to send a message of gratitude and adoration to the Creator Son [30:4.28].

5. Paradise Arrivals

Residence on Paradise means that one has found God and will be mustered into the Mortal Corps of the Finality [30:4.31]. After a period of liberty the arrivals associate with the seven groups of primary supernaphim, and on completing the course with the conductors of worship they are assigned, as Paradise graduates, to finaliter service [30:4.32]. The book says that their present destiny alone fully justifies the universe plan of evolutionary ascension [30:4.33].

Summary

The mortal ascender begins as a planetary mortal and, if necessary, passes through the stage of sleeping survivor, then advances as mansion world student, morontia progressor, superuniverse ward, Havona pilgrim, and Paradise arrival [30:4.2-4.8]. Along the way the body changes from material to morontia to spirit, while mind, personality, and character continue [30:4.20, 30:4.26]; this outline is the average plan in effect in Nebadon and Orvonton [30:4.34].

q190.question: Besides ascended mortals, what beings make up the Mortal Corps of the Finality, and how is a single company organized?
q190.answer:
The Urantia Book introduces the Mortal Corps of the Finality as the present known destination of the ascending Adjuster-fused mortals of time, while making clear that this corps is not made up of mortals alone [31:0.1]. The primary Corps of the Finality consists of six groups, Havona natives, Gravity Messengers, glorified mortals, adopted seraphim, glorified Material Sons, and glorified midway creatures, and the seventh place is still vacant [31:0.2-0.8, 31:7.3].

These diverse beings are organized according to their experience of working together during the ascension career; all are received on an equal footing, but that equality does not abrogate individuality or personal identity [31:0.9].

1. The Organization of a Company

The corps is organized in companies of one thousand, consisting of one Havona native, one Gravity Messenger, and nine hundred and ninety-seven ascendant creatures [31:1.3]. Of these, the Adjuster-fused mortals and the adopted seraphim usually make up nine hundred and ninety, the mortals far outnumbering the seraphim [31:3.1]. There are just ten places in each company for beings who are neither mortals nor seraphim: the Havona natives, the Material Sons, the midway creatures, the Gravity Messengers, and the unknown member [31:3.1]. At present every company has nine hundred and ninety-nine sworn permanent members, and the vacancy is temporarily filled by the chief of the Evangels of Light [31:7.1].

2. The Havona Natives and the Gravity Messengers

The Mortal Corps of the Finality admits as permanent members only beings who have fused with the spirit of the Father, or beings like the Gravity Messengers who inherently embody that spirit [31:1.2]. The Havona natives must therefore achieve, in liaison with evolutionary beings, the experiential development that creates capacity to receive a fragment of the Father's spirit, and they are received in the ratio of one to a thousand [31:1.2, 31:1.3]. The possibility of becoming finaliters is one of the supreme adventures of this perfect race [31:1.4]. The Gravity Messengers are modified and personalized Adjusters from Divinington, superspirit beings who seem to utilize all energies and circuits, even gravity [31:2.2]. They are under the command of the finaliters, and between them and the mortal finaliters fused with fragments of the Father there is profound mutual affection [31:2.1, 31:2.4].

3. The Adopted Seraphim, the Material Sons, and the Midway Creatures

Many of the faithful seraphic guardians of mortals pass through the ascension career with their wards, become Father fused, take the finaliter oath together with them, and forever accept the destiny of their mortal associates [31:4.1]. Material Sons may embark on the ascent by petition when their planetary assignment is long delayed, or may become humanized, receive Adjusters, and ascend in the later ages of light and life; when they are in a finaliter company they are always chosen as leaders [31:5.1-5.3]. The midway creatures begin their ascent after their native world has been settled in light and life, and the secondary midwayers all eventually fuse with Adjusters and are mustered into the mortal corps [31:6.1, 31:6.2].

4. The Evangels of Light and the Vacant Seventh Place

Any celestial personality assigned to the service of the Corps of the Finality is called an Evangel of Light; these are temporary members who do not take the finaliter oath [31:7.2]. There are at present just six classes of permanent members, and as to the identity of the seventh group, even the beings on Uversa can only offer various speculations [31:7.3-7.5]. The finaliters are a self-governing body that chooses its own leaders, and they swear allegiance only to the Paradise Trinity [31:0.12]. The book calls them the tried and true souls of time and space, "⟦Q 31:0.13⟧the evolutionary salt of the universe⟦/Q⟧" [31:0.13].

Summary

The Mortal Corps of the Finality is made up mostly of Adjuster-fused mortals and adopted seraphim, together with Havona natives, Gravity Messengers, and glorified Material Sons and midway creatures, while the seventh place for permanent members is still vacant [31:0.2-0.8, 31:3.1, 31:7.3]. A company numbers one thousand, filled by nine hundred and ninety-nine permanent members and the chief of the Evangels of Light as a temporary member [31:1.3, 31:7.1]. What characterizes this corps is that beings of different origins form one body on an equal footing while each keeps his own identity [31:0.9].

q191.question: Why did God not make human beings perfect from the start, but have them evolve and ascend from lowly beginnings?
q191.answer:
Paper 32 of The Urantia Book answers this question head-on. It would have been just as easy for the Universal Father to make all mortals perfect beings and to impart perfection by his word, but that would deprive them of "⟦Q 32:3.11⟧the wonderful experience of the adventure and training associated with the long and gradual inward climb⟦/Q⟧" [32:3.11]. That experience is to be had only by those who begin at the very bottom of living existence [32:3.11].

Evolution, then, is not a sign of God's incapacity or indifference but a way that reveals the wisdom of the Creators [32:3.11], and the whole universe is designed so that the creatures who "receive" perfection and the creatures who "achieve" perfection complement each other [32:3.12].

1. Outside Havona, Perfection Is Achieved Progressively

The only settled creation is Havona, made directly by the thought of the Universal Father and the word of the Eternal Son, while the seven superuniverses are finite, evolutionary, and steadily progressive [32:3.1]. The physical systems of time and space are all evolutionary in origin [32:3.2], and except for the central universe, perfection is a progressive attainment [32:3.3]. Havona holds the pattern of perfection, and all other realms must attain that perfection by the established methods [32:3.3].

2. Acquired Perfection Is a Bona Fide Personal Possession

The book says that the perfection achieved by the creatures of time is "⟦Q 32:3.9⟧wholly an acquirement, a bona fide personality possession⟦/Q⟧" [32:3.9]. Though the elements of grace are freely admixed, the attainment is the result of individual effort and actual living, the reaction of personality to the existing environment [32:3.9]. Thus the fact of animal evolutionary origin attaches no stigma to any personality, and those who begin at the bottom and climb the ladder rung by rung receive greater honor and an actual knowledge of every phase of life [32:3.10]. There is truly no limit to the spiritual ascent of those who are indwelt by the Mystery Monitors [32:3.8].

3. The Mutual Complement of Inborn and Evolved Perfection

The experiential nature of evolving personalities is the natural complement of the ever-perfect nature of the Paradise-Havona creatures [32:3.12]. Perfect creatures and perfected creatures are both incomplete in finite totality, but when they are associated together they escape their inherent limitations [32:3.12]. The two are alike in degree of divinity potential but differ in kind, and each must depend on the other to attain supremacy of service [32:3.14]. Inborn perfection and evolved perfection are co-ordinate, dependent, and integrated [32:3.15].

4. The Eternal Purpose within Evolution

There is a great and glorious purpose in the march of the universes through space, and none of the struggles of mortals are in vain [32:5.1]. The events of time and the struggles of material existence are but the transient scaffolding that bridges over to spiritual realities [32:5.2]. In the mind of God there is a plan that embraces every creature, and this plan is "⟦Q 32:5.7⟧an eternal purpose of boundless opportunity, unlimited progress, and endless life⟦/Q⟧" [32:5.7]. Yet because in the lower stages of progress it is difficult to find the invisible Father with the eyes of faith, the book counsels that the surest safeguard is to hold persistently to the truth that the Father is present in his Sons [32:3.6].

5. What It Means for Our Lives

This teaching shows us that the immaturity and struggle we experience are not signs of failure but the process by which perfection becomes "our own." The book promises that the race for perfection is on, that whosoever will may enter, and that the crown of victory will be placed on every effort to run the race of faith in reliance on the guidance of the indwelling Adjuster and the Spirit of Truth [32:5.8].

Summary

God did not make us perfect from the start in order to give us the adventure and training of beginning at the bottom and acquiring perfection through experience [32:3.11]. The perfection thus gained is a bona fide personal possession [32:3.9], and in partnership with the inborn perfection of Havona it fulfills the larger purpose of the universe [32:3.12, 32:3.15]. The path of evolution is a journey that is not in vain within the eternal plan of God [32:5.1, 32:5.7].

q192.question: In the administration of the local universe of Nebadon, what position does each of Michael, Gabriel, and Immanuel hold, and what does each do?
q192.answer:
Paper 33 of The Urantia Book explains the government of our local universe of Nebadon around three personalities. Michael of Nebadon, the Creator Son, is the sovereign who chose to organize this universe and now supremely rules it [33:2.2]; Gabriel of Salvington, the Bright and Morning Star, is the chief executive of Nebadon [33:4.5]; and Immanuel of Salvington, the Union of Days, is the ambassador of the Paradise Trinity [33:5.1].

Put simply, Michael rules, Gabriel executes, and Immanuel represents Paradise and counsels. Knowing the relationship among the three lets us see how the local universe runs in good order.

1. Michael: Sovereign and Personification of the Father-Son

Michael's personal power is limited only by the gravity circuits centering in Paradise and by the reservation of the Ancients of Days of final judgment regarding the extinction of personality [33:2.2]. The book says, "⟦Q 33:2.3⟧Michael is the personification of the Paradise Father-Son to and in the local universe of Nebadon⟦/Q⟧" [33:2.3]. When he returned from his final bestowal on Urantia and the Mother Spirit subordinated herself to him, he acquired jurisdiction over all power in heaven and on earth [33:2.3].
